#1564. Newcastle a challenge but a good post-Interlull opportunity

Arsenal are back in Premier League action after the Interlull with a trip to face Newcastle away from home. It’s been a difficult place to visit over the years, and we’ve had some unenjoyable encounters – there particularly during Eddie Howe’s tenure. However, Mikel Arteta more or less has a full squad to choose from, and this version of Newcastle under new manager Matthias Jaissle haven’t been at all convincing so far this season.

In terms of the Arsenal team today, Arteta can flip a coin between Ben White and Jurrien Timber, both of whom were on the scoresheet for their countries during the break. My gut feeling is that the Dutchman will start today with White penciled in for Borussia Dortmund in midweek. William Saliba is back after another behind closed doors appearance to build his fitness, but for a game that’s likely to be intense and physical, I can’t see anything other than Ezri Konsa alongside Gabriel today. The Frenchman often needs a game or two to get his rhythm back, and while friendlies are useful, they’re not quite the same as competitive minutes. He too is likely to feature in the Champions League on Tuesday.

In midfield there’s no Martin Zubimendi whose unfortunate run of injuries continues with a hamstring strain picked up playing for Spain against England. The form of Declan Rice and Martin Odegaard means they’re first picks, and then it’s about how the manager views Bruno Guimaraes for a game like this. Even if Newcastle haven’t been great, the pantomime villain in midfield adds a layer of spice that is inevitable after his summer move. If he wants to keep the crowd quiet, he could choose Myles Lewis-Skelly, but he paid £75m for this player for a good reason, and I think we’ll see the Brazilian from the start.

He was a hugely important player for Newcastle, and while I don’t think his departure was among the most contentious we’ve ever seen, he will be a target for their fans, and perhaps for players who know him – and his temper – very well. You’d hope at 28 he’s mature enough to deal with all that, and I’m sure conversations will have been had about not rising to any bait. Arteta has said more than once recently he wants more from this player, where better to give that than his former club?

As for the front three, I think it will be Christos Tzolis and Noni Madueke either side of Kai Havertz. The injury news for Bukayo Saka means he’s going to miss another month, at least, so there’s a big onus on Madueke to continue his recent improved form, but we’ll need him to add end product to the one goal and one assist he’s provided in the league so far. Similarly, Tzolis had a bright-ish start to his Arsenal career, and while the hamstring injury was ill-timed, we need a player who is ostensibly our first choice left winger to start delivering more in terms of assists but especially goals.

Havertz got the winner away to Liverpool, but had frustrating moments at home to Hull. He’s got Viktor Gyokeres on the bench to put some pressure on him, but this front three has some convincing to do and today would be a very good day to produce performances and end product.

Arteta was asked if the atmosphere at St James’ Park isn’t quite what it used to be, because of the way the team has changed and the inconsistent form they’ve suffered so far this campaign. His message was clear:

If that’s the case, it will be even more difficult, because they will be even better prepared, they will have even more necessity to do that, and that’s what we expect. We always expect the best version from the opponent. That’s how we have to prepare for the game, and that’s how we’re going to approach it.

So, there’s no chance he’s letting his team think for a second this might be easier because it’s not the same Newcastle that have caused us problems in recent seasons. Nevertheless, he must have looked at this team and some of the issues they’ve had under their new manager and recognised that this is an opportunity to go there with a settled side of his own in good form and come away with all three points.

It is always a challenge there, but this is a mature Arsenal that should be capable of dealing with a team that has just three wins from thirteen games in all competitions this season. You never take anything for granted, but if we can keep the ball in the early stages, get control, and perhaps even an early goal, the ingredients are there for us to make this a winning start to what is a tricky run of games over the coming weeks. Fingers crossed.

Right, I’ll leave it there for this morning. As ever, we’ll bring you live blog coverage of the game later, as well all the post-game stuff on Arseblog News like the match report, player ratings, manager reaction, quotes round-up and more. There’s also a preview podcast on Patreon if you need something to listen to ahead of kick off. Don’t forget the updated Arseblog apps also have a cool new matchday centre, full of stats, alerts, and much more.

#1561. Newcastle 2-2 Arsenal: Two points dropped in a game of two halves

In the cold light of day, it’s hard not to look at what happened in the 45th minute of this game as a key moment. Arsenal were 1-0 up, well on top and absolutely deserving of the lead. Newcastle had struggled to exert any kind of control, and we’d already had 9 attempts on goal.

A good move down the left hand side saw Martin Odegaard square perfectly for Noni Madueke who arrived with pace, ready to finish first time. Unfortunately for him and for us, Lewis Hall produced a quite outstanding piece of defending to slide in and block the shot over the bar. That was the difference between Arsenal going in 2-0 up at the break rather than with just the single goal margin.

The lead had come via Eberechi Eze, finishing emphatically after superb work from Kai Havertz to rob the ball and play a deft pass behind the right back. Newcastle’s only chance had come early, a shot from Jacob Murphy that deflected off his own player and drifted wide with David Raya wrong-footed. After that, we bossed the half, with 11 shots in total, 65% possession, but still only that one goal.

It feels redundant to say this is a very, very good Arsenal team, but if we have a weakness, it’s that we don’t turn this kind of domination into more goals. Very often we don’t need to as our defensive solidity and consistency keeps the opposition at bay, but last night we let our standards slip in that regard, and the lack of firepower or being clinical in the final third came home to roost.

It was, very literally, a game of two halves. Newcastle made a triple sub at the break and it would be churlish not to give them credit for the fact it made a positive impact. However, the Arsenal performance was night and day. The opposition upped the energy and intensity, and we made mistakes. Odegaard miskicking a Riccardo Calafiori throw-in provided them the opportunity to equalise, and I do wonder why Harvey Barnes was so free at the back post to slide home for 1-1.

That goal gave them momentum, they caused us problems again and again, some of them of our own making with carelessness and misfortune. Eze got back well to defend in our box but unfortunately slipped, Raya’s clearance was unconvincing and then Gabriel had to boot the ball behind for a corner – from which they made it 2-1. Dan Burn drifted off Jurrien Timber to get a free header, the ball scrambled around a bit before Malick Thiaw poked it over the line to give them the lead. Messy, shambolic defending – not very Arsenal at all.

If we’re being fair, we have to say they could have scored again. David Raya went off with a shoulder injury, Kepa had to make a smart save at the feet of Lewis Miley but why was he one on one with the keeper in the first place? A Joe Willock shot deflected wide in similar fashion to the Murphy one in the first half, and eventually Arteta changed things with Christos Tzolis and Myles Lewis-Skelly coming on for Eze and Bruno Guimaraes who had a quiet return to his former club – bar that first half moment when he almost got enough contact on a fantastic Declan Rice cross but could only put the ball wide from close range.

We did get an equaliser, and very well worked it was too. We played the ball across the back line from right to left, into midfield where Havertz’s smart dummy allowed Odegaard room to drive on and find Madueke. He was Arsenal’s best attacking player last night, he kept trying to make things happen, and while I think the Newcastle keeper will probably have nightmares about letting that shot in, Madueke deserved the goal, and it earned us a point.

It was after the 90th minute when the manager brought on Viktor Gyokeres and Mikel Merino to try and find a winner, the Swede had one shot over the bar from the edge of the box, but had we found another, it would have been a real smash and grab. In the end, the draw was probably a fair result based on how the game played out, and afterwards the manager was unhappy at leaving two points behind:

My feeling is that we have lost two points today. And I say we because we were exceptional in the first half, from the beginning to the end. It should have been two, three or four-nil up, clear. But it wasn’t.

We started to lose duels, we started to lose second balls. We gave the ball away and have really poor circulation balls against their press and their waves. And when that happens, you give them belief.

It’s a pity because the margin should have been, again, much bigger for the level that we’ve shown.

And this is the key for me. It should have been, but it wasn’t, and it too often isn’t. As I said above, our defensive brilliance is fundamental to us winning so many games, but football is a game of variance. You can’t always control everything. On another night Odegaard just puts his foot through that throw in and that first Newcastle goal doesn’t happen. Eze and Raya deal better with that situation and we don’t concede a corner. We can focus on those individual things and say we could and should do better for sure, but you have to allow for some of that over the course of a season. You cannot be perfect for 90+ minutes 38 games in every league campaign.

The ongoing issue for me is our firepower though. I thought generally the front three played pretty well last night, and it’s not as if we missed a glut of chances, but it’s about turning the level of dominance we had in that first half into more goals. This isn’t a one-time issue either. We scored two lovely goals last night but we should have had that game firmly in our grasp at half-time, but in this league a single goal margin is never a sure thing.

The summer was a let-down in an attacking sense, there’s no getting away from that. If we had a forward line that was even close to our midfield and defence in terms of quality and depth, the Premier League would be a cakewalk. I know that’s a bit simplistic, but it’s also a fact. Regardless of what you think of the business, we let goals go to Turkey and Saudi Arabia, and replaced them with a player who has yet to score. Which isn’t to lay the blame at the feet of Tzolis, far from it, but with the squad planning/building that was undertaken.

For me, January becomes increasingly important because the improvement required is obvious, and for a sporting director whose track record looks quite hit and miss as it is, he needs a convincing window or the questions around the job he’s doing will become louder and louder, and for good reason.

The other big issue from yesterday was the injury to David Raya. It didn’t look good at all, and any absence for him would be a huge blow to the team. He’s been the best in the Premier League, and perhaps the best in Europe, for the last 18 months, and inevitably there’s a drop-off when any club is without their first choice keeper for any period of time. That’s another adjustment we’re probably going to have to make, and if it means we’re likely to be less secure and clean sheets are harder to come by, then that issue of scoring goals and being more potent comes into even sharper focus. Let’s keep fingers crossed it’s not as bad as it appears to be.

Right, I’ll leave it there for now. There’s plenty to unpick from this one, so I’ll leave you to it in the Arses. More here tomorrow, including an Arsecast Extra. Until then, have a great Sunday.

#1559. Mind the gap

Over the last few weeks, I’ve grown accustomed to waking up and experiencing low-level fear first thing in the morning. Today, it was a nice change not to be focused on my own health, and instead for my anxiety to centre around someone else – David Raya.

With any team or any squad there are players whose absence will be more keenly felt than others, but one of the things Arsenal have generally done really well in the last few years is close the gaps between ‘first choice’ and those behind them. It doesn’t mean there isn’t still a kind of hierarchy, just that you’re better able to cope if injury or suspension hits. Mikel Arteta referencing ‘finishers’ rather than substitutes might be a psychological ploy to keep his squad happy, but it’s more easy to apply when you have the group of players he has at his disposal.

If Jurrien Timber is out, we have Ben White. If Riccardo Calafiori can’t play, Piero Hincapie can. We all worried about William Saliba needing a long lay-off after the World Cup, but the arrival of Ezri Konsa offset that in exemplary fashion. If we miss Declan Rice, we have two World Cup winners, a Brazilian international, and one of the most highly regarded young English midfielders around to fill that gap. Further forward, Noni Madueke is performing at a level that makes Bukayo Saka’s absence feel less impactful than it would have previously, and while I think forward line quality remains an issue we need to solve as urgently as January, you can flip a coin between most of our options there without feeling you’ve weakened yourself considerably.

Unfortunately, I don’t think the same applies between the sticks. Raya has been the stand-out goalkeeper of the last few years, establishing himself as Arsenal’s number 1 after an initial settling in period. One, by the way, which I don’t think the manager handled particularly well. Typically he’s been near flawless in terms of his man-management, and while he was fundamentally right about wanting the Spaniard to come in and take the position to a new level, the way he fudged things around Aaron Ramsdale, talking about how he’d sub a goalkeeper in a game and all that nonsense really wasn’t his best moment. It left both of his keepers in a weird place for too long, until Raya’s confidence grew and his quality came to the fore.

Since then he’s won multiple golden glove awards, his shot-stopping has been incredible at times, and although every player and every keeper will make mistakes, his have been few and far between. For me though, despite the eye-catching acrobatics – which are more easily clipped up for the social media generation – his key asset is the assurance he brings to the team. Not just when he has the ball at his feet (even if there are times I would like him to move it more quickly), but how good he is from opposition set-pieces and crosses. He comes and claims and eases pressure time and time again, and I think that’s the thing we’re going to miss most if he’s out for any significant period of time.

Kepa is obviously a very experienced second choice, but is second choice for a reason. Realistically though, I don’t think there’s much any club can do to have a back-up option that’s nearly as good as their number 1. If you’re being brutally honest, many clubs in the Premier League don’t have a first choice that comes anywhere close to be as good as Raya, despite their best efforts and spending millions to try and find that player. So, as anxious as I am about him being out, it is one of those things we can’t really complain about. We just have to get on with it.

As I said in yesterday’s blog, we are probably going to be less secure at the back, that feels kind of inevitable, so the onus on the players further forward increases. Score more goals, turn that domination of possession and territory into more chances. If we have the ball in their half, our goalkeeper becomes something of a non-issue for as long as that’s the case. There are ways to cope, but we might need to gird our loins for some iffy moments at the back that we haven’t had to experience too often of late.

As Arsenal fans though, we’ve come through worse than this with goalkeepers in the past. I don’t want to give anyone PTSD first thing on a Monday morning, but when you’ve lived what we’ve lived in seasons gone by, hopefully a little Kepa period won’t be too traumatic. And maybe, after the scan, there’ll be better news about Raya than we expect. Fingers crossed.

Right, I have to leave it there for this morning. We will have an Arsecast Extra for you a bit later on though. We’ve already put out the call for questions on BlueSky @gunnerblog.bsky.social and @arseblog.com, so fire away using the hashtag #arsecastextra – or if you’re an Arseblog Member on Patreon, leave your question in the #arsecast-extra-questions channel on our Discord server.

Pod should be out around noon. Until then!

#1557. Liverpool transfer news: Reds 'ready to battle' for £37.7m attacker familiar to Jurgen Klopp

By Oliver Thomas | 24 Nov 2026 12:22

Liverpool are reportedly among a number of clubs interested in signing Borussia Monchengladbach wonderkid Wael Mohya.

Earlier this month, the 17-year-old attacker earned his first-ever senior international call-up to Jurgen Klopp’s Germany squad after making a notable impression as a first-team regular at club level.

Mohya broke into Monchengladbach’s senior side midway through last season and became the club’s youngest-ever goalscorer against Bayern Munich in March of this year.

He has since developed into an increasingly influential player under head coach Alexander Blessin this term, featuring in all 10 Bundesliga matches as well as two DFB-Pokal games.

Mohya became the fourth youngest-player in Bundesliga history to score in consecutive games in October, contributing with a goal and an assist in a standout display in a 3-2 win against Stuttgart.

The dynamic and versatile attacker, who is comfortable operating centrally or out wide, has produced several impressive performances that have subsequently caught the eye of some of Europe’s biggest clubs.

According to TEAMtalk, Andoni Iraola’s Liverpool have shown concrete interest in Mohya and have intensively scouted the teenager.

The report adds the Reds are ‘ready to battle’ with high-flying Brighton & Hove Albion, who currently sit second in the Premier League table and have also been closely monitoring the attacker.

Bundesliga giants Bayern Munich, Borussia Dortmund, Bayer Leverkusen and RB Leipzig are also said to be keeping an eye on Mohya’s progress, while Real Madrid, Barcelona and AC Milan are some of the big clubs abroad who have recently entered the race for his signature.

As things stand, Monchengladbach are yet to receive any formal offers for Mohya or enter negotiations with another club despite growing interest in his services.

Mohya’s contract is due to expire in June 2028, and Monchengladbach sporting director Rouven Schroder recently insisted that “he is definitely not for sale in January,” adding: “The rest will depend on how the market develops.”

The youngster is viewed as a key part of Monchengladbach’s plans for this season, and it is understood that an offer in the region of €45m (£37.7m) is what it would take to persuade the German club to open talks over a possible sale in the coming transfer windows.

#1555. Dortmund a tricky test + Guimaraes on getting to grips with Arteta’s midfield

Arsenal are in Champions League action this evening, taking on Borussia Dortmund at home. It’s a game that Kepa Arrizabalaga will start in the absence of David Raya, but the news around the Arsenal number 1 was a little more positive than expected. In his press conference yesterday, Mikel Arteta said:

He’s not fit for tomorrow, unfortunately, but it doesn’t look too serious. We need some more tests tomorrow, but it’s quite encouraging. With the pain that he was showing immediately after the action, we were all quite worried, but he seems to be better than what we expected.

We expected something much worse because he could almost not handle the amount of pain that he had at that moment, and the first test that we’ve done showed something that is much more encouraging. There’s no need for surgery, which was the main fear especially because that would rule him out for months, so let’s see.

So, it seems like he’s going to miss a few games, but not anything prolonged, which is obviously good news. Elsewhere, there’s room for rotation, and I think this might be a good chance to give minutes to William Saliba who hasn’t played competitively since the World Cup.  He’s had a couple of behind closed doors appearances, which will be useful in terms of fitness, but nothing compares with actually playing at this level.

I wonder too if players like Ben White, Cristhian Mosquera and Piero Hincapie will fancy their chances, but that seems like a lot of change in the back four – and the goalkeeper – so we’ll have to wait and see there. In midfield, we can bring Myles Lewis-Skelly in for a start, but obviously the manager has plenty to choose from in there, and up front I imagine it will be a chance for Viktor Gyokeres whose minutes have been scant so far this season. Asked if the striker had been knocking on his door about that, Arteta said:

No, we have conversations with every player to make sure that they understand what we are doing, to gather information about the way they are feeling, and so far, it’s been very positive with Viktor and with the rest of the team.

He could really use a goal tonight if he does start, as does Christos Tzolis whose numbers so far this season aren’t where you’d like them to be. Obviously there’s more to assessing a player than simply goals and assists, but for a left winger brought into replace two players who contributed a lot to the team over the last few seasons, just two assists from 11 appearances (Community Shield excluded) is a little below what you’d hope. He has had an injury, of course, but if his season needs a kick-start, tonight would be very timely.

Dortmund sit top of the Bundesliga right now, unbeaten in the league thus far, and with just one defeat all season in all competitions. That did come in the Champions League, away to Bodo Glimt, but this will be a tricky test tonight for Arsenal. Arteta says:

I’m very impressed with them, you see the results so far, where they are in the Bundesliga at the top and where they are in the Champions League and especially the way they are playing, the way they are dominating games, the amount of threat they are able to create. We had them here in pre-season, and they showed the quality and what they are capable of, so we are very much aware of that. But we play at home in front of our crowd, and now we’re going to go and attack the game, that’s for sure.

After a disappointing second half against Newcastle on Saturday, I’m sure the manager will be looking for a response from his side. It’s nice to be at home again, and a long spell of games in London will hopefully less taxing physically without all the travel, so it’d be good to get that off to a winning start tonight.

Elsewhere, Bruno Guimaraes spoke about his first few months at the club, and how he now feels like he’s getting to grips with what Mikel Arteta wants from him, saying:

I’m here, I don’t know, three, four months? It’s still a lot to go, but I now definitely understand my role in the team, the way that Mikel wants me to play in the team. So, yeah, I think I still can play much, much better.

And it’s quite interesting to hear him talk about how at Arsenal he is more ‘free’ than he was under Eddie Howe at Newcastle. Most would feel it was the other way around, but he explained:

It’s very different. When I was at Newcastle, you play more positional, keep more your position. Here it’s a little bit more free.

If you see the game against Newcastle, they were marking us man to man. You see JT [Jurrien Timber] plays a six, an eight and a number nine sometimes, so you have to move a lot. Of course, I was not used to it. So now I understand a little bit more what he wants for the midfield.

I think there’s more to come from him, he’s looked good at times, a little off the pace at others, and I think my main worry is about the physical side of his game. Does he have the running power and athleticism that enables players like Declan Rice and Martin Odegaard to thrive under this manager? At 29, he’s no spring chicken, but I guess there’s always room for improvement. Anyway, his press conference stuff from yesterday is worth reading, and there’s some good chat about him on the Arsecast Extra which you’ll find below.

Right, I’ll leave it there for this morning. #1554. Torreense vs Celtic - prediction, team news, lineups

By Ellis Stevens | 24 Nov 2026 12:23

Torreense welcome Celtic to Estadio Municipal de Leiria on Thursday night for a matchday five clash in the league phase of the Europa League.

The hosts are 19th in the standings with six points from four games, while the visitors are 32nd with three points after four matches.

Torreense made history by defeating Sporting Lisbon 2-1 in the Taca de Portugal final last season, marking the club's first major trophy and securing their qualification to the Europa League.

Torreense, as a result, became the first non-top flight club to qualify for the revamped league phase of the competition, and Azul-grenas have performed admirably in their opening four fixtures.

Thursday's hosts have secured two wins and suffered two defeats in their first four games, leaving Torreense placed 19th in the league phase table and on course to qualify for the knockouts.

The latest of those victories, a dramatic 3-2 win against Ararat-Armenia that featured two goals in stoppage time to come from 2-1 down to secure the win, came under new boss Joao Nuno, who was appointed after Luis Miguel Valado Tralhao mutually agreed to step down as manager.

Nuno recorded one win and one draw in his first two games, but the manager has since suffered back-to-back defeats heading into this match, leaving Torreense eager to avoid enduring a third consecutive loss.

Torreense will draw confidence from their impressive displays in the Europa League, while visitors Celtic have shown signs of weakness in this competition this term.

The Bhoys have won only one of their four league phase fixtures, alongside three defeats, scoring just six goals and conceding a considerable 11 goals in that time.

Martin O'Neill's side actually lost each of their first three league phase fixtures, results that coincided with a miserable run across all competitions, during which they recorded six defeats, one draw and just three wins between mid-September and the beginning of November.

However, a 3-2 triumph over Besiktas on matchday four of the league phase, featuring an 87th-minute winner from Camilo Duran, has sparked a three-game winning run, subsequently defeating both Kilmarnock (1-0) and St Mirren (4-1).

Celtic will be looking to extend that winning streak and secure just their second win of the league phase on Thursday, with the Bhoys hoping to move closer to the qualification places.

While Celtic have returned to winning ways in recent matches, concerns remain about their form on the road, having lost three of their last five away fixtures across all competitions.

Torreense will be without Jorge Aguirre for Thursday's fixture after the forward was sent off in the matchday four clash with Ararat-Armenia, and Adama Baradji is also not expected to feature due to an injury concern.

In Aguirre's absence, Musa Drammeh, who scored in the defeat to Benfica last time out, should lead the line, with Carlos Reina providing support in attacking midfield.

Meanwhile, Duran, who has scored 14 goals in 22 appearances for Celtic this season, should lead the line, with Sebastian Tounekti, Benjamin Nygren and Haissem Hassan providing attacking support.

Further back, Alex Oxlade-Chamberlain and Callum McGregor could feature at the base of midfield, with Cameron Carter-Vickers and Liam Scales in central defence.

Although Celtic have struggled on the road in recent matches and shown signs of weakness in the Europa League, the away side should have the quality to overcome their second-division hosts and secure the win.

#1552. Report: Liverpool transfer target is '100% out' in January, he'll cost €50m

Liverpool aren't in the best run of form at the moment.

The Reds are miles away from first-placed Arsenal and, right now, it doesn't feel like they have the quality among their ranks to get back to the top of the Premier League table.

Fans expected Liverpool to be challenging for the title this season, especially after their £150 million + spend in the summer.

That obviously hasn't worked out with fans now questioning whether the club even has enough strength among their ranks to get them where they need to be.

Right now, the January transfer window is just over a month away and, fans are expecting a lot of change to take place.

So, the fact that one of their reported targets are '100%' on their way out of Anfield is a very good sign.

Barcelona are '100%' going to sell Alejandro Balde in January

Since the arrival of Ronald Araujo, Liverpool's defence has been fairly solid.

The Uruguayan has brought an extra layer of stability to Andoni Iraola's ranks and has helped take a lot of pressure off the shoulders of Jeremy Jacquet.

Thanks to how strong Araujo has been, Jacquet has been allowed to take his time to settle into Premier League life and, he's probably been one of Liverpool's best signings thanks to that.

Right now, it's unclear what the Reds' priorities are going to be in January but, thanks to an update from journalist Juan Jesus, a bit of a better insight has now been given to fans.

"Despite Deco’s words, Alejandro Balde is 100% out. Several clubs know this and are closely monitoring his situation, including Manchester United, PSG, AC Milan and Liverpool," he shared via X.

"Barça expects the bidding to drive up the price and is confident of securing his departure for at least 45–50 million euros."

Alejandro Balde's new price tag is expensive

When talk of Liverpool being linked with Balde first emerged, the deal was pitched as an unmissable offer for the Reds.

Talk of a deal worth around £30 million was being mooted with other clubs such as Manchester United also linked with an interest.

However, the fact that the deal could end up costing around €50 million (£41.9 million) makes things a little harder to understand.

Obviously, Balde is an incredible player and would help solve two of the Reds' main issues going into 2027.

But, £41.9 million is a lot of money for the club to spend on another left-back.

Everyone thought that Milos Kerkez was going to be the second coming of Andy Robertson after he was signed for £40 million but, in reality, he still needs to do a lot of work to improve his game.

Right now, it's unclear what plans Liverpool have for the upcoming transfer window but, if they don't make a couple of meaningful signings, by the end of the 2026-27 season, they'll be fighting for a Champions League place, rather than the title.

#1551. GdS: ‘Numbers like Kaka’ – why Rabiot is so important to Milan with renewal imminent

Adrien Rabiot has had an outstanding start to the 2026-27 season, and he is showing absolutely no signs of slowing down.

La Gazzetta dello Sport (seen below) begin a report this morning by pointing out what Rabiot said after Milan’s 5-1 demolition of Frosinone on Sunday: “An assist is better than a goal.” He was the man of the match against Frosinone: five goals were scored, yet none bore his name.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Still, the Frenchman made himself the stand-out performer, thanks to his tireless running, leadership, and a series of decisive passes, not to mention his role in the opening goal, which came via an own-goal.

It was a summer of doubts for Rabiot, given that his extended vacation was interpreted by some as a sign of discontent and a longing to reunite with his former mentor – Massimiliano Allegri – at Napoli. Yet, he has transformed into a cornerstone of this new era.

The former PSG man is now a decisive force on the pitch, integral to Ruben Amorim’s tactical framework, and a true leader. The numbers demonstrate this perfectly: Rabiot is the first midfielder to contribute to at least one goal (scoring or assisting) in seven consecutive Serie A appearances since Kaká in 2004.

With five goals and six assists, he recently became the first midfielder in the last 20 years of Serie A to record more than 10 goal contributions within the first 10 matches of a single season. In total, Rabiot has surpassed the milestone of 50 direct goal involvements in Serie A (29 goals and 22 assists).

Milan trust him, and the feeling is mutual. As previously mentioned, the very fact that he remained with the Rossoneri over the summer – publicly reaffirming his commitment to the club – is reflected in his attitude, both on and off the field.

Adrien Rabiot – Goal Contributions so far

12 G/A in 14 Games https://t.co/s8oTle9GBn

He is always smiling and highly active on social media; his numbers on Instagram are as impressive as his stats on the field. He posts photos of his goals, his celebrations and embraces with Diego Moreira, with whom he is clearly building a close bond.

Amorim said after the game: “Adrien can play as a ’10,’ an attacking midfielder, an ‘8,’ or even as a playmaker – though he doesn’t particularly like that role. He is certainly one of the best players I have ever coached, and one of the best midfielders in Europe.”

Speaking to Telefoot, Rabiot addressed the topic of his excellent start statistically: “It’s a positive thing to have players capable of being decisive, even if they aren’t forwards. It also serves as an encouragement to those around us.

“At Milan, we have quite a few young players, and it’s important for them to have role models in their day-to-day lives. I had only been back from vacation for a week when he was already talking to me about a contract renewal.

“I told him, ‘Coach, take it easy!’ (laughs). But, naturally, it’s significant for a player to feel that kind of trust—the coach relies on us, holds us in high regard, and makes us feel important.”

Further significant remarks regarding Rabiot were made by Gerry Cardinale on the eve of the most recent league match, specifically concerning his imminent contract renewal.

“I love Adrien, he’s one of my favourite players. He’s fantastic. I have enormous respect for him and his family. We are in talks, and I hope we reach a happy conclusion soon. I believe he should be a signature player for Milan. Could it be a Christmas gift for the fans? Absolutely, and for me, too.”

The renewal will happen, and it will happen soon. Any delay until the new year should not be interpreted as a negative sign. Rather, it reflects the fact that everything is already settled, and there is no rush to finalise the signature.

Adrien’s current deal – which runs until 2028 – will be extended to 2030, with an additional one-year option. From his current age of 31, he will remain a fixture in the Rossoneri midfield until he is 33 or 34, the prime of his footballing maturity.

Now into his thirties, he will also earn a more lucrative contract than his current one, which pays him €3.5m net per season. It is worth noting that in the summer of 2025, Adrien was acquired from Marseille for €7m after a training-ground altercation with Jonathan Rowe.

It was, by any definition, a fantastic deal. As for the future, Rabiot has a role model he can observe from very close quarters: “Modrić trains as if he were 21, he’s an example to follow. The closer you get to the end of your career, the more you start to savor every moment. I try to do the same.”

With the imminent contract extension, Adrien Rabiot is also set to conclude his career in the red and black colours, and that would make everyone happy.

#1550. Chelsea news: £75m player seriously considered retirement under Enzo Maresca

By Oliver Thomas | 24 Nov 2026 12:42

Chelsea defender Wesley Fofana has admitted that he seriously considered retiring from football during Enzo Maresca’s time in charge at Stamford Bridge.

The one-cap France international joined the West Londoners from Leicester City for a reported £75m in the summer of 2022 and has since played 81 times for the club across all competitions.

Fofana’s career at Chelsea has largely been disrupted by injury, missing a total of 41 matches during Maresca’s 18-month reign with the Blues.

While Fofana began the 2024-25 season fit after recovering from a year-long ACL tear, two major hamstring injuries wiped out nearly six months of his campaign.

The 25-year-old centre-back has since opened up about how the psychological strain that came with a rash of injuries almost led to the decision to prematurely call time on his career.

Speaking in an interview for Zack Nani TV, as quoted by the Evening Standard, Fofana said: “There was a period when I was recovering from my cruciate ligament and meniscus injuries.

“Then I suffered two consecutive hamstring strains under Enzo Maresca, when I really decided: ‘That’s it, I’m retiring, I’m done playing.’ I was serious.

“I really wanted to stop, because, for the first time in my life, I wasn’t happy anymore. It wasn’t just about being injured or not playing; my whole life was completely shattered. I wasn’t myself anymore. I sincerely believed that, in the future, I would only get injured.

“I thought to myself: ‘That’s it, football isn’t for me, I’m too fragile.’ I even used Abou Diaby as an example. I thought to myself: ’I guess I’m the Abou Diaby of our generation. There has to be someone like that, and it happened to me. It’s my destiny, I accept it.’”

Fofana added: “Of course, I was very sad and didn’t want to stop, because I was living my dream. At that point, I called my agents so we could sit down and talk, telling them, ‘Okay, I’ve decided to retire.’

“They started analysing the situation with me, talking about contracts and all that: ‘It’s simple, you still have several years left on your contract, and there’s a lot of money to be made.

“Even if you really decide to stop playing, you still have to come every day, keep smiling, and even if you’re injured, you have to honour your contract for your future.’

“But at that moment, I really felt that the pain football caused me far outweighed the joy, so why continue? I was in pain almost 100 per cent of the time.

“Every time I gritted my teeth, played a few games, and just started to find a little love and joy in life again, bang, I’d get injured again.”

Fofana has since made positive progress in building up his strength and fitness; he played 38 times for Chelsea in all competitions last season and has started seven of the first 11 Premier League matches under new manager Xabi Alonso so far this term.

Last month, Alonso publicly backed Fofana as an "important," "focused," and "mature" first-team figure, who is under contract at Stamford Bridge until the summer of 2029.

#1548. Journalist: Andoni Iraola refused to strike deal for World Cup star

Liverpool head coach Andoni Iraola reportedly refused to strike a deal for a World Cup star over the summer. He got his wish - and was absolutely right.

Andoni Iraola didn't have the easiest job when he took over as Liverpool head coach in the summer. He inherited a squad that was incredibly expensive - by far the most in the Reds' history - but wasn't playing well.

Wasn't playing well at all, actually. Liverpool's points last season were generated through individual efforts rather than team play, surviving on the fact they had more talent than their opponents.

The potential was always massive, then, but the pressure was high and it was completely unclear if the group could actually play together. Moreover, Liverpool intended to spend even more over the summer and would lost some incredibly important players.

It's now November and we're still completely unclear whether this group can play together. But things are promising. And you've got to say that some of that promise is thanks to Iraola putting his foot down.

Alisson Becker's contract technically expired last summer, but Liverpool triggered an option in the deal that extended it for an extra year. Their plan at one stage appeared to be that they'd extent it so they could sell Alisson for a bit of money before they lost him for free.

Juventus were heavily interested in signing Alisson. It certainly appeared that a deal would go through, too, only for things to fizzle out and for the goalkeeper to remain with Liverpool this season.

It appears that Iraola played a large role in that happening. Journalist Nicolo Schira reports that Iraola considered Alisson to be non-transferrable and wouldn't let him depart the club.

What a decision that was. Alisson has had a tremendous start to the season, firmly re-establishing himself as no.1 and one of the best goalkeepers on the planet right now.

On top of that, Iraola kept one of the most experienced players at the club - something incredibly important with all this turnover each summer. It was unquestionably the correct decision.

And one that looks like it might result in committing to more years of Alisson. Schira says that Liverpool are in talks to get a new contract signed, potentially extending things to 2029. And to say we're behind that decision would be an understatement.

#1546. Report: Liverpool send scouts to eye European sensation, Man City also want him

Andoni Iraola and Julian Ward have cast their net far and wide to find new players for Liverpool to target.

During the 2026-27 summer transfer window, over £150 million + was spent on new players to try and bolster the Reds' ranks.

And, while some of them moves have worked out well, others haven't.

This inconsistency among Liverpool's ranks has massively impacted the way that things have gone for them this season.

Right now, they're fourth in the Premier League table but, if they want to get back to the top and start challenging for silverware, they're going to have to spend even more money.

So, that's why many new players seem to be getting linked with Liverpool all the time.

Liverpool and Manchester City want to sign Yunus Akgun

One area that Liverpool heavily focused on improving in the summer was their attack.

Bradley Barcola and Victor Munoz were signed in the summer transfer window just gone and, the season before that, Alexander Isak, Hugo Ekitike and Florian Wirtz were all brought in.

And, while all of these additions looked good on paper, some of them just haven't kicked on with Liverpool still needing to add some new faces to their ranks.

Many different players have been presented as options to Liverpool over the last couple of months but now, thanks to an update from X account Mekteb-i Gala (who have over 50,000 followers), Galatasaray attacker Yunus Akgun is now on Liverpool's radar.

"EXCLUSIVE | PSG, Manchester City, Liverpool, Atletico Madrid, Como and Juventus are monitoring Yunus Akgün in every match," they wrote.

"They are in the process of gathering information on the player."

Yunus Akgun could be a cheap option for Liverpool to explore

Since Yunus Akgun is 26 years old, he's a tad older than most of the Reds' recent targets.

A lot of Liverpool's transfer plans over the last couple of years have consisted of signing young players for the future.

This has been proven by the recent arrivals of Munoz, Barcola and Wirtz.

And, while all of these players are good enough to feature in Liverpool's starting XI now, the fact that they have potential to become even better is extremely exciting.

Indeed, Akgun isn't at the end of his career yet but, after he contributed to 21 goals last season and has already scored four goals this term, it's unclear if he's already reached his peak or not.

The fact that he can be used as a left-winger or a number 10 is also another major selling point of the attacker.

No fee was mentioned for Akgun but, of all the players who have surfaced as potential options recently, the Turkiye international who's appeared 25 times for his country, looks like one of the most exciting.

#1545. OFI Crete vs Anderlecht - prediction, team news, lineups

By Matt Law | 24 Nov 2026 12:49, Last updated: 24 Nov 2026 12:52

Anderlecht will be aiming to make it three straight wins in the league stage of the Europa League when they travel to OFI Crete on Thursday night.

The visitors will bring a four-game unbeaten run in all competitions into this match, but Crete will enter the European fixture off the back of a 2-0 loss to Panathinaikos in the Greek Super League.

OFI have a record of two wins and two losses from their four matches in the league stage of this season's Europa League, with six points leaving them in 16th position in the overall table.

The Club started their league phase with a 2-0 win over Hoffenheim before losing back-to-back games in the competition against Rennes and Bayer Leverkusen.

However, Christos Kontis' side posted a 2-0 victory over H. Beer Sheva in their last Europa League game on November 5, so they will be aiming to make it back-to-back wins in the tournament.

OFI are playing in the league stage/group stage of a major European tournament for the first time since the 1995-96 campaign, and this is also the first time that they have ever qualified for this round of the UEFA Cup/Europa League.

The Club have European matches to come against Benfica, Sturm Graz and Lech before the end of the group stage in early 2027.

Anderlecht, meanwhile, have also won two and lost two of their four matches in this season's Europa League league stage, with six points leaving them 15th in the table.

The Belgian club started their league phase with a 2-1 loss to Lyon, before going down 1-0 to Dinamo Zagreb in the middle of October, but they have won their last two matches in the tournament against Jagiellonia and Red Bull Salzburg to move onto six points.

Vitor Bruno's side will enter this match off the back of a 1-0 win over Leuven in the league, with the result leaving them in fifth position in Belgium's top flight.

Anderlecht will face Hoffenheim, Sunderland and Marseille in their three European matches after this one, and it would be a surprise if they were not present in the knockout round.

The Purple and Whites won this competition back in 1982-83, and this is their first Europa League league phase campaign since 2024-25.

Meanwhile, there should also be a position in the side for Thiago Nuss, who has provided seven goal contributions in all competitions for Crete this term.

As for Anderlecht, Ilay Camara and Lucas Hey are out of the match due to injury problems.

Mihajlo Cvetkovic has been in strong form for his Belgian club this season, scoring seven goals and registering two assists in 22 matches, and the 19-year-old will continue in the final third of the field.

There are also expected to be spots in the final third for Danylo Sikan and Jayden Onia-Seke.

#1544. “Annoyed” Kevin De Bruyne faces uncertain Napoli future ahead of Man City return

By Oliver Thomas | 24 Nov 2026 13:05

Manchester City legend Kevin De Bruyne is preparing for an emotional homecoming at the Etihad Stadium on Tuesday night, though his current spell with Napoli has been clouded by transfer speculation and internal friction.

After winning 19 trophies during a glittering 10-year career at Man City, the 35-year-old playmaker reluctantly left the club at the end of the 2024-25 season when the decision was made to not extend his contract.

De Bruyne subsequently signed for Napoli as a free agent, embarking on a fresh challenge in Italian football, but his debut campaign was struck by injury, starting only 16 matches across all competitions as Napoli surrendered their Serie A crown to Inter Milan.

The Belgium international has since played in all 16 games for Napoli across Serie A and the Champions League this term, chipping in with four goals and two assists while operating in a deeper midfield position under head coach Massimiliano Allegri.

De Bruyne is part of an aging Napoli side that are currently languishing down in eighth place in Serie A and sit 27th in the Champions League standings after losing three of their opening four League Phase games.

Tensions boiled over during Napoli’s heavy 4-1 UCL loss at Porto earlier this month, where teammates had to separate De Bruyne and striker Lorenzo Lucca following an angry on-pitch row.

"Speaking about the pitch, De Bruyne is the best player this year at Napoli. The point is that the whole team is having difficulties, Naples-based journalist Vincenzo Credendino told BBC Sport.

"We saw that there is a problem, at least between De Bruyne and Lorenzo Lucca. Their acting was very, very clear and I think that in that time, the two of them were wrong.

"On one hand you cannot swear at another team-mate but on the other hand, De Bruyne reproached Lucca without encouraging him, so it was a bad show."

As De Bruyne enters the twilight years of his career, it has been suggested that the “spark never really ignited” between the midfielder and the Naples outfit, raising uncertainty over his future at the club.

When asked about his future at a press conference ahead of Napoli’s Champions League clash with Man City, De Bruyne said: "Not a lot I can say for the moment. I have played at 100% until now and obviously I am not 20 years old, I am turning 36.

"There is a lot of things going in my mind but there is not a lot to say. I am playing good football, trying to help the team to do well and it has been a bit of a challenging season with a lot of things happening."

De Bruyne will soon be entering the final six months of his Napoli contract and will be free to negotiate pre-contract agreements with foreign clubs in January.

De Bruyne has also expressed his annoyance over the backlash he and his family have received following controversial comments made by the player’s wife in September.

His wife Michele reportedly told Belgian magazine NINA about their desire to move back to Belgium, saying "the sooner we get there, the better" as De Bruyne leads a "very restricted life" in Naples.

Addressing the media fallout, De Bruyne replied: "To be honest, I am pretty annoyed because if you read the article, that none of you have read, to understand what she said.

"I was away in Belgium and a lot of noise came and a lot of bad reactions to my wife and family. I saw pictures of my house, I don't think it is OK but it is what it is and some press created this in Italy. I don't know why.

"Nobody knows my life, you will never know. People who work with me are not allowed to say anything but obviously it is something that I take away and think about. It has not been nice for my wife or for my family."

De Bruyne has since been linked with a sensational Premier League return in January, while Dutch giants PSV Eindhoven are understood to have failed with a €2m (£1.7m) opening offer to sign him in the New Year, with Napoli valuing the midfielder closer to €8m (£6.7m), according to Credendino.

Napoli boss Allegri has interestingly refused to rule out a mid-season departure for De Bruyne, stating on Monday that transfer decisions are "down to the players and who wants to leave" once January arrives.

Meanwhile, De Bruyne has spoken out for the first time since Man City were found guilty of breaching Premier League financial regulations.

By Ben Knapton | 24 Nov 2026 13:08

Liverpool have confirmed their 22-man travelling squad for Wednesday's Champions League clash with Club Brugge at the Jan Breydel Stadion.

The Reds are going in search of their fourth win from five continental matches in Belgium, having overcome Atletico Madrid, Villarreal and LASK Linz before a 3-2 loss at Fenerbahce last time out.

Andoni Iraola's men have responded to that setback with back-to-back Premier League wins, though, following up a 3-1 triumph at Crystal Palace with a 4-0 battering of Manchester United on Sunday.

Teenage starlet Rio Ngumoha stole the show against the Red Devils in the absence of Cody Gakpo, who was an unexpected absentee from Sunday's matchday squad due to a calf injury.

Iraola revealed that Gakpo suffered his injury while on international duty with the Netherlands, and the attacker has not been included in the travelling party for Wednesday's game.

Gakpo's problem is not believed to be serious, though, and there is a chance that he will be fit to return for the weekend's Merseyside derby with Everton at the Hill Dickinson Stadium.

As well as Gakpo, compatriot Ryan Gravenberch will also miss Liverpool's trip to Brugge, as the midfielder continues his recuperation from a small heel fracture.

After the weekend's win over Man Utd, Iraola expressed hope that Gravenberch would be fit for the Champions League clash, having returned to training while carefully managing his pain.

However, the Netherlands international will now miss a fourth consecutive game for Liverpool, and he is still waiting for his first minutes of November, having also been an unused substitute against Arsenal.

Gravenberch and Gakpo are two of five Liverpool absentees against Club Brugge, as Hugo Ekitike (Achilles), Giovanni Leoni and Conor Bradley (both knee) have not made the cut either.

The rest of Liverpool's squad is as expected, and alongside Ngumoha, five other Kirkby youngsters could earn opportunities to impress at the Jan Breydel Stadion.

Published: 22:41 EST, 21 November 2026 | Updated: 03:57 EST, 23 November 2026

Inter Miami star Lionel Messi was lucky not to have been sent off after hurling the ball in the face of his opponent during an embarrassing MLS Cup Playoff defeat.

In the Round of 16 contest against the Columbus Crew, Miami went down 1-0 early in the first half with a penalty converted by Gonzalo Tapia. The deficit was then compounded when Miami fullback Gonzalo Lujan was sent off with a second yellow card.

On the stroke of halftime, Messi nearly joined his teammate in the locker room with a moment of madness on a throw-in.

Tapia and Messi were both standing out of bounds as the Chilean striker prevented the World Cup winner from taking his throw right away.

Messi then used the ball to shove Tapia's face back. When the Columbus man tried jumping in the air to block the throw, Messi then threw the ball into Tapia's head.

Tapia crumbled to the ground as Messi raised his hands asking for a foul on the Crew star.

Lionel Messi takes a throw-in off Gonzalo Tapia's face pic.twitter.com/jX3tTuojHe

Lionel Messi nearly got sent off during his team's MLS Cup Playoff match against Columbus

A frustrated Messi launched the ball off the face of Crew striker Gonzalo Tapia as he prevented the Argentina star from taking a quick throw in. Both players received yellow cards.

Tapia got revenge by scoring a brace to lead the Crew to a 3-0 victory on Saturday evening

Referee Allen Chapman was not happy with either player's antics, showing yellow cards to both Tapia and Messi.

But ultimately, Columbus and Tapia would get the last laugh as they won 3-0 in the best-of-three Round of 16.

Midfielder Taha Habroune scored the second goal of the evening in the 52nd minute as Tapia secured a brace just six minutes later.

The result has Inter Miami on the brink of elimination from the playoffs after winning the title last season. Columbus dominated every facet of the game, thanks in part to owning 62 percent of possession.

Messi attempted two shots on the evening – counting for half of the saves from Crew keeper Patrick Schulte.

Inter Miami must win the next match in Ohio to stay in the playoffs. If the game finishes tied, the rules dictate the match will proceed directly to penalty kicks.

Out of his three prior seasons in the United States, Messi's 2025 MLS Cup victory was an outlier. Miami missed the playoffs in 2023 and were eliminated in the first round in 2024.

#1537. Exor pays in €60m of Juventus’ €250m raise, but UEFA deal limits January plans

Juventus shareholders have cleared a capital increase of up to €250m, and majority owner Exor has already committed €60m of it. Giovanni Carnevali warned that the UEFA settlement means nothing extraordinary should be expected in January.

Juventus shareholders gave the board the power to raise up to €250m in new capital at the Allianz Stadium on 3 November. The vote came in the extraordinary part of the meeting and passed with 99.9% in favour. The same assembly approved the 2025/26 accounts.

Part of the money is already committed. Exor has already paid in €60m as an advance towards the capital increase. That payment supports the club’s equity and finances until the board uses its new authority. The majority owner has also guaranteed its own 65.4% stake in the raise and any shares other investors leave untaken.

The squad will not see the full sum. Shoring up the club’s finances across this season and next will take 45–50% of whatever is raised, according to Football Italia. That leaves roughly €100m mainly for first-team signings before the January window. Beyond keeping equity at a suitable level, the rest will go on controlling debt and keeping the team competitive, including transfers, Corriere dello Sport reports.

The accounts show why the balance sheet needs support. The consolidated loss for 2025/26 was €66.0m. That was €7.9m bigger than the previous year’s €58.1m. The result was in line with the forecasts in the club’s half-year report to 31 December 2025. The board had approved the accounts on 29 September. Another loss is expected in 2026/27, mainly because Juventus are in the Europa League rather than the Champions League.

The assembly was Giovanni Carnevali’s first as chief executive. He promised a serious approach to the January window. His warning was just as clear. As a serious company, Juventus must honour its settlement agreement with UEFA and does not expect to do anything extraordinary.

That agreement was announced on 30 June. It is a three-year settlement with the First Chamber of UEFA’s Club Financial Control Body. It relates to Juventus breaking UEFA’s Football Earnings Rule over the three seasons from 2022/23 to 2024/25.

For supporters, the message is mixed. The capital increase gives the club fresh resources. The settlement still dictates how quickly that money can be used on the pitch.

Shareholders also criticised the club for keeping a low profile in recent years. President Gianluca Ferrero declared Juventus open to dialogue with Tether.

The terms of the UEFA deal leave little margin. Missing the targets agreed with UEFA for the current season or the next two can lead to limits on the club’s UEFA List A and further sporting sanctions. The settlement runs until the 2027/28 financial year.

#1534. Harry Kane injury leaves Bayern Munich considering unlikely return

By Axel Clody | 24 Nov 2026 13:51

Just when his European career seemed to belong to the past, Eric Maxim Choupo-Moting could return to one of the biggest clubs in the world. Bayern Munich are studying a return for the Cameroonian forward to cover temporarily for the absence of Harry Kane.

Eric Maxim Choupo-Moting definitely has the art of appearing where no one expects him. At 37, after two seasons in Major League Soccer, the Cameroon international is among the solutions being considered by Bayern Munich to strengthen their attack this winter.

According to Sky Sport Germany, the former Paris Saint-Germain man's name was raised internally after Kane's injury. The Bavarian club do not have a genuine replacement centre-forward and are studying several options before the January transfer window. No final decision has been made yet, but the Cameroonian's candidacy exists.

A free agent at the end of his deal with New York Red Bulls, Choupo-Moting would be willing to sign for only six months, until the end of the season. He would also accept returning to the bench once Kane has recovered, without asking for any special status.

This profile has several advantages for Bayern Munich. The Cameroon international knows the club, its environment and the demands of the Bundesliga. He could be available immediately and would not need a long period of adaptation. Signing him would be a low-risk solution to accompany Kane's gradual return.

The mere fact that the Munich hierarchy are thinking of him says a lot about the esteem he left in Bavaria. Between 2020 and 2024, Choupo-Moting scored 38 goals in 122 appearances in all competitions. Initially signed to back up Robert Lewandowski, he managed to become a starter and to deliver when the Pole left the club.

After leaving for MLS following the end of his first spell at Bayern Munich, the Cameroonian made a successful start in New York. In 2025, he scored 17 goals and provided five assists in 33 regular-season games.

His playing time decreased in 2026, but he still scored five goals and provided one assist in only 538 minutes across 21 games. These figures show that his efficiency has not disappeared, despite a role that has become secondary.

This American stay could have been the quiet final stage of an already full career. Choupo-Moting could make the opposite journey and return to the Champions League, the Bundesliga and a dressing room he knows inside out.

Long reduced to a few famous misses during his time at Paris Saint-Germain, Choupo-Moting has built a career that few players can claim. Schalke 04, Stoke City, Paris, Bayern Munich and then New York: everywhere, he ended up getting playing time and making himself useful.

His honours include several French and German league titles, and he played in a Champions League final with Paris Saint-Germain. A return to Munich would be yet another snub to those who have often presented his presence at big clubs as an anomaly.

Two of the main positions that the Reds need to upgrade this winter are their left-back and centre-midfield.

Both positions have players among them that haven't met expectations at all this term.

This has led to a lot of underperformance from Liverpool and has forced them to continually experiment with the players that they have at their disposal.

In some cases, players such as Trey Nyoni and Lewis Koumas have massively benefitted from this but, in others, questions remain.

Many different players are on the Reds' shortlist but now, an update from journalist Juan Jesus may have just confirmed who the Reds' main targets could end up being.

"In addition to Alejandro Balde, Barça are now pushing Gavi out this very winter to fund the signing of a centre-back, seen as the club’s absolute priority," he wrote.

"The main target to bolster the defence is Nico Schlotterbeck, but the current wage bill leaves no room to pull off a move of that magnitude in January.

"To comply with financial fair play rules and try to sign him in this winter window, the board is pushing for two key sales: Balde on one hand, and the bombshell departure of Gavi on the other."

Gavi and Alejandro Balde would be two perfect signings for Liverpool

Most Liverpool fans will know that Balde has been linked with the Reds for a while now.

The Spaniard has been left out of Hansi Flick's plans this term with the La Liga giants making it clear since the summer window slammed shut that the 23-year-old had no future left at the Camp Nou.

His natural position is left-back but, he's also been used as a right-back in the past.

Gavi is a completely different kettle of fish altogether. The 22-year-old has played in 179 games throughout his career so far with his best position being a central midfielder.

During his time in Barcelona's first-team squad, he's helped Pedri boss many different midfields and has contributed to 28 goals across all competitions.

Right now, it's unclear how much either of them would cost but, since the Reds' relationship with Barcelona is strong, a deal could definitely be agreed.

#1528. Spalletti skips Fiorentina preview as Juventus seek a first win over Vanoli

Luciano Spalletti will not hold his eve-of-match press conference before Sunday's trip to Fiorentina. Juventus arrive on two straight wins, chasing fourth place, against a coach Spalletti has never beaten.

Juventus will travel to Florence without the usual preview from their coach. Sunday’s game at the Franchi kicks off at 20:45. The squad got back to Turin overnight from the Netherlands. The reason given is the club’s crowded run of fixtures, TuttoJuve reported. It is the last game before the international break.

The run began with a 2-0 win over Napoli at the Allianz Stadium on 1 November. Kerim Alajbegovic scored in the 70th minute. Aged 19 years and 41 days, no foreign player had ever found the net at a younger age in a Serie A game between Juventus and Napoli.

Four days later, Juventus won 2-1 away at AZ Alkmaar in the Europa League. Teun Koopmeiners and Randal Kolo Muani scored. The result takes them to 10 points from four games in the competition. After the match, Spalletti described himself as very pleased with a solid team display against strong opponents. He felt his side should have added a third goal.

The league position still needs work. The club’s stated aim this season is fourth place, and Como currently hold that spot. The defence gives some grounds for confidence. Going back to last March, no side can match the Bianconeri’s tally of 12 shutouts. Roma are next on 11.

Vanoli and Spalletti have faced each other only twice as coaches. Both meetings were Fiorentina-Juventus fixtures last season. Last November they drew 1-1 at the Franchi. Filip Kostic gave Juventus the lead before Rolando Mandragora equalised with a long-range shot.

The hosts’ struggles on their own pitch offer Juventus an opening against a side yet to find its footing at home.

The fixture carries plenty of history. Sunday’s game is the 175th Serie A meeting between the sides, according to the club’s statistical preview. Juventus have won 82, Fiorentina 37, and 55 have ended level. Juventus have scored 275 top-flight goals against Fiorentina. Two more would draw them level with Inter’s 277, the highest total by any side against the Viola.

Once the international break is over, Juventus’s next Serie A match is on 22 November.

By Jonathan O'Shea | 24 Nov 2026 15:08, Last updated: 24 Nov 2026 15:10

Seeking to extend their unbeaten run through this season's Europa League, Juventus will welcome Omonia to Turin on Thursday evening.

While Juve are on track for automatic qualification to the last 16, their visitors are bound for the knockout playoffs as things stand.

More accustomed to Champions League football, Juventus have made a strong start to their campaign in Europe's second tier, claiming 10 points from a possible 12 so far.

After a 5-0 cruise at home to NEC, the Italian giants secured victory over Celta Vigo on matchday two, before playing out a 2-2 draw against Rennes.

Last time out, they retained a top-eight spot by beating AZ in Alkmaar, where Teun Koopmeiners scored against his former club in a tense 2-1 win.

Since then, results have somewhat improved in Serie A, after Juve had made an inconsistent start; four points from two games have lifted Luciano Spalletti's side up to sixth place.

Having fought back twice to salvage a draw with Fiorentina, they then put four goals past lowly Venezia, inspired by Nick Woltemade's half-time introduction from the bench.

However, Spalletti's injury-hit squad still trail 11 points behind league leaders Lazio, while Italy's tight top-four fight could go all the way.

Before facing fellow contenders Como on Sunday, Juve will aim to maintain their undefeated home record in the Europa League, having won six games and drawn nine in Turin since the competition began.

Juventus have also won all four prior meetings with Omonia Nicosia, beating them over two legs in both the 1977-78 European Cup and the 1999-00 UEFA Cup - the Cypriot side lost 10-2 on the latter occasion.

While Juve sit fifth in the Europa League table on 10 points, Omonia's tally of six leaves them 18th midway through the league phase, so defeat could see them drop into the elimination zone.

After coming through qualifying, then winning two of their first three games, Henning Berg's side suffered a 3-1 defeat to NEC on matchday four, despite seizing the lead through Lois Diony's opening goal.

Since that setback, they have beaten Anorthosis Famagusta and drawn 1-1 with city rivals APOEL, with Diony scoring on both occasions. As a result, the Nicosia club are fifth in the Cypriot top flight, five points shy of the summit.

Their domestic title defence may not be going to plan, but Omonia are on track to escape a Europa League group or league phase for the first time to date - albeit potentially via the playoffs.

Juventus still have a long absence list, and Kerim Alajbegovic is set to join it on Thursday evening, after picking up a minor thigh problem against Venezia.

Pierre Kalulu and Nico Gonzalez are expected to return from injury this weekend, but Kenan Yildiz, Khephren Thuram, Kamil Grabara and captain Manuel Locatelli are still sidelined.

Newcastle United loanee Woltemade now has nine goal contributions for the Bianconeri, having either scored or assisted in all four Europa League appearances.

Likely to support Randal Kolo Muani up front, the German striker also ranks second for shots attempted and for open-play chances created in this season's league phase.

Meanwhile, French forward Diony should lead Omonia's attack, after scoring in three consecutive matches.

Though Hungary international Loic Nego recently returned from a layoff, Carel Eiting is still ruled out by a long-term knee injury.

#1523. Bremer earns Juventus 2-2 draw at Fiorentina but leaves them six points off Champions League places

Gleison Bremer's equaliser earned Juventus a point at the Stadio Artemio Franchi after they twice fell behind against Fiorentina. Spalletti's side now go into the international break outside the Champions League places, with their next home game brought forward by a day.

The point leaves Fiorentina 15th in the table on 9 points.

The hosts led after four minutes. Mateo Pellegrino scored, set up by Pedro Goncalves. Nick Woltemade levelled in the 32nd minute from a Randal Kolo Muani assist, and it was 1-1 at half-time.

Fiorentina went ahead again in the 54th minute. Guglielmo Vicario made the first save, but the Juventus defenders were too slow to clear. Alieu Njie forced in the rebound. Bremer then reached a Douglas Luiz corner in the six-yard box before David de Gea could get to it.

Juventus completed 384 accurate passes to Fiorentina’s 273. Fiorentina still attempted 22 shots to Juventus’s 18, and both sides had 6 on target. The expected goals figures, 2.46 for Juventus and 2.14 for Fiorentina, are consistent with a fairly even contest despite the visitors’ control of the ball.

The closing stages could have gone either way. Former Juventus defender Radu Drăgușin headed in from a corner in the 82nd minute. The goal was ruled out because he pushed Bremer with both hands. Near the end, Vicario saved twice in quick succession to protect the point. Juventus also claimed a penalty when the ball struck João Mário’s arm in the Fiorentina area, but none was given.

Referee Andrea Colombo booked three Juventus players. Juan Cabal was cautioned in the 13th minute and Bremer in the 22nd. Kolo Muani was booked for dissent in the 73rd. Christ Inao Oulaï was Fiorentina’s only booking.

Juventus were without the injured Kenan Yildiz, Andrea Cambiaso, Nico González, Manuel Locatelli, Khéphren Thuram and Kamil Grabara. Weston McKennie and Zeki Çelik returned to the squad. Spalletti made three changes in the 57th minute, sending on Zhegrova for Woltemade, Alajbegovic for Boga and Celik for Cabal. Ekhator replaced McKennie in the 78th minute and Gatti came on for Lucumí in the 89th.

At his press conference at the Franchi, Spalletti said he was not happy because his team does not play at a steady enough level to aim for anything important. He did praise Kolo Muani, describing him as the player everyone wanted and one he can use as a centre-forward or out wide. Shown a replay of the João Mário incident, he dodged the question and asked, smiling, for a different one.

The draw ended a run of two wins, against AZ Alkmaar and Napoli. Woltemade and Pellegrino both received a rating of 8.2 from the data provider.

Next up for Juventus is Venezia, who sit 19th on 6 points. When fixture times were first set, that game was pencilled in for Monday 23 November at 20:45 Italian time.

#1522. Olympiacos vs AC Milan - prediction, team news, lineups

By Jonathan O'Shea | 24 Nov 2026 16:29, Last updated: 24 Nov 2026 16:43

Ailing giants AC Milan must try to kickstart their Europa League campaign on Thursday evening, when they visit Olympiacos at Stadio Georgios Karaiskakis.

Despite their status as seven-time European champions, Milan are on course for early elimination, while their unbeaten hosts have only dropped two points so far.

Milan will head into the second half of the league phase with a point to prove, having lost three out of four games to date - including the last two without scoring.

Recently beaten by Bournemouth and Ferencvaros, Ruben Amorim's side have failed to even find the scoresheet since Goncalo Ramos struck in their lone win against Red Bull Salzburg.

A paltry tally of three points leaves the Italian heavyweights in real danger of being knocked out, as they sit 28th in the Europa League table and only the top 24 will go through.

By contrast with their continental results, Milan are showing clear signs of progress in Serie A, where they occupy fourth place, just ahead of city rivals and reigning champions Inter.

The Rossoneri have taken 15 points from the last available 18 - while scoring at least twice on each occasion - and they have only lost one domestic fixture this term.

Aiming to keep pace in the Scudetto race, Amorim's men hosted surprise high-flyers Frosinone last weekend, when they eventually cruised to a 5-1 win, with rising star Alphadjo Cisse scoring again.

However, Milan must now head to Greece, where they memorably won the 1994 Champions League final but have never beaten native hosts in six prior attempts.

In particular, Milan's two previous visits to Piraeus ended with a 2-2 draw in 1959 and a 3-1 defeat in 2018, when Olympiacos won the most recent meeting.

That was also in the Europa League, and the Greek giants currently sit sixth in this season's league phase - seven points clear of the Rossoneri.

As things stand, Olympiacos will directly enter the last 16, despite losing their perfect record last time out.

Across all competitions, they had won nine straight games before being held to a 0-0 draw by Rennes, which followed victories over Jagiellonia Bialystok, Marseille and Sparta Prague.

All told, Imanol Alguacil's side have lost just one of their last 18 fixtures, and Sunday's 6-2 destruction of 10-man Iraklis left them second in the Greek Superleague standings.

Furthermore, Olympiacos have only suffered one defeat in their last 13 Europa League matches - while keeping nine clean sheets - so they will surely fear no-one on home turf.

Amorim has typically shuffled his lineup for Europa League games - albeit not to positive effect - and several fringe players should feature for Milan.

Omari Hutchinson and Ardon Jashari have often played, while Cisse could start again; the new Italy international already has six Serie A goals and he scored a hat-trick away to Salzburg earlier in the campaign.

At the other end of the spectrum, experienced captain Mike Maignan can return after serving a one-match ban for his red card against Bournemouth.

Goncalo Ramos is set to overcome a minor calf problem, but the visitors must travel without Mattia Gabbia, Fikayo Tomori, Samuel Chukwueze, Alexis Saelemaekers and Ruben Loftus-Cheek due to injury.

Meanwhile, Olympiacos are missing long-term absentees Ayoub El-Kaabi and Yusuf Yazici, plus South American pair Gustavo Puerta and Santiago Hezze.

Leon Bailey bagged two goals and an assist at the weekend, so he could link up with Armando Gonzalez, who is the hosts' top Europa League scorer with two.

Portuguese playmaker Jota Silva has racked up the most shots in this season's league phase; however, just two of those 17 attempts have found the target and none have hit the net.

Ortega; Saliakas, Retsos, Carmo, Onyemaechi; Freuler, Scipioni; Bailey, Silva, Fortounis; Gonzalez

Maignan; Gila, De Winter, Pavlovic, Diawara; Musah, Jashari; Hutchinson, Rabiot, Cisse; Ramos

Milan may have struggled to score in Europe, but with Amorim developing an exciting front line, they average above two goals per game in Serie A and are overdue to convert some chances.

That said, Olympiacos are a formidable force on home soil, so they can keep their unbeaten streak going with a hard-fought draw.

#1520. Juventus Next Gen beaten 4-0 at Lecco and left third from bottom

Juventus Next Gen were beaten 4-0 at Lecco in Serie C Girone A, with three of the goals coming after half-time. Coach Massimo Brambilla admitted his young side give goals away too easily, and the table now reflects a long poor run.

At the Stadio Rigamonti-Ceppi, the manner of the defeat was as worrying as the scoreline.

The opener set the tone. Lecco needed only six minutes to go ahead. Casarotto ran through the middle, got past Corradi and beat goalkeeper Mangiapoco. Lecco held that single-goal lead until half-time.

Next Gen did have one clear opening before the break. In the 40th minute, Grelaud shot from near the penalty spot. Vettorel turned the effort over for a corner.

The second half was one-way traffic. Capello made it 2-0 in the 50th minute, and Manetti added a third in the 56th. Capello struck from close range after the goalkeeper parried Pellegrino’s second attempt. Murillo’s goal in the 72nd minute summed up the match. Mangiapoco erred as Juventus built from the back, and Murillo pounced.

The hosts are in strong form. This was their second 4-0 win in a row, after beating Dolomiti Bellunesi by the same score. Lecco have now scored 15 goals in four games.

Massimo Brambilla did not hide from the problems. He told TuttoMercatoWeb that his side struggled against Lecco’s high press. His players found it hard to keep the ball against a team pressing hard and man-to-man.

The coach also admitted that coming back became difficult after the second goal. He said his players must improve how they read the game and stop giving away goals so easily.

The table makes the warning sharper. Brambilla’s side sit third from bottom after the defeat, having won just one of their last 12 matches.

The result also matters beyond Serie C. Carnevali has put the youth sector at the centre of the club’s plans.

One player supporters will watch is Destiny Elimoghale, who came off the bench at Lecco. Next Gen had started in a 3-5-2, with Durmisi and Merola in attack.
