#1481. Juventus sell out Venezia game as Omonia sales pass 35,000

Juventus have sold out Sunday's Serie A home game against Venezia despite a long injury list. Strong early sales for the Europa League visit of Omonia Nicosia keep the club in line for another strong European crowd.

Juventus go into Sunday’s home game against Venezia still short of players. Several remain unavailable for Sunday’s 12:30 kick-off. Edon Zhegrova has trained with the group and is considered available. Celik, Cambiaso, Nico Gonzalez and Kalulu remain out, Sport Mediaset reported. For Spalletti, a full home crowd arrives in the middle of a busy run of games.

General sale for the fixture opened at 3pm on Tuesday 6 October. Supporters living in the province of Venezia could buy only if they held an active Juventus Card. The fixture belongs to the 2026-27 Serie A Enilive season.

This season every Juventus match ticket is digital. Each one is managed through the Allianz Stadium App.

Season-ticket holders who cannot attend can list their seat on resale.juventus.com. The club, not the seller, sets the resale price. A few of those listings are now all that remains for supporters who missed the general sale, ANSA reported.

The season-ticket terms also reward turning up. To keep first refusal on a 2027-28 season ticket, a holder must use the seat for at least 70 per cent of matches. That means at least 13 of the 19 league games.

The Europa League has drawn big numbers to Turin this season. Against NEC, 39,308 match tickets were sold, with away fans counted separately. No away figure was released for the Rennes visit, but that section was full.

The Rennes game finished 2-2 on 22 October. Juventus needed a second-half Woltemade penalty to draw after trailing 2-1.

Omonia Nicosia are next. Bookings for the Cypriot club’s visit still trail the two earlier European crowds.

Juventus have set strict conditions for the fixture. Supporters of Cypriot nationality may buy tickets only for the away section. The club has warned that breaking UEFA rules can lead to cancelled tickets and refused entry.

Taken together, the figures are consistent with a home support that keeps buying despite the injury list. The weekend league fixture will be followed by a European night that is already well on its way to another large crowd.

Juventus host Omonia Nicosia in the Europa League on 26 November.

#1480. Arsenal transfer news on Germany winger: Is second choice enough?

Arsenal transfer news: Arsenal like Kevin Schade, but he isn’t the winger they want most. Football.London’s Tom Canton reports that the Brentford forward is on the shortlist for the left flank, with RB Leipzig’s Antonio Nusa ranked above him. Canton says the 24-year-old Germany international is certainly appreciated at the Emirates.

The ranking reflects an awkward summer for Mikel Arteta. Arsenal sold Leandro Trossard and Gabriel Martinelli, missed out on Vinicius Junior and signed only Christos Tzolis for about £34m.

Tzolis started the first five league games, then suffered a hamstring injury on international duty. Eberechi Eze and Noni Madueke have covered since, and Madueke rescued a point in Saturday’s 2-2 draw at Newcastle, which left Arsenal six points clear for now.

Nusa, the 21-year-old Norwegian winger, has six goals and eight assists in 15 matches for Leipzig. Sky Sports reports that the Bundesliga club won’t sell him in January, so a summer deal looks more realistic, with Leipzig reportedly valuing him between £60m and £77m. Schade is the quicker route, but Arsenal asked about him in the summer and got nowhere, according to TEAMtalk. His contract runs until 2028.

Schade has scored three times in ten Premier League appearances from 2.44 expected goals, and his pace suits a side that already creates through Tzolis. He can play either flank or centrally. The weaknesses show elsewhere: no assists, three chances created in 781 minutes, seven completed dribbles at a 25% success rate and 43.8% of duels won. FotMob values him at about £47m.

Not in January, and certainly not as a consolation. Arsenal lead the league, Tzolis remains the first-choice left winger, and Madueke has just shown he can deliver there. Schade would add depth, but he wouldn’t add what Arteta lacks: a winger who beats his man and drags two defenders with him against low blocks.

Nusa builds his game on exactly that, and his output at Leipzig now justifies waiting until next summer. Schade’s returns suggest he would sit behind a fit Tzolis, which is hard to justify at a price Brentford would set after already refusing an approach.

A bid becomes sensible only if Tzolis breaks down again or Leipzig block Nusa completely, because Schade needs no time to adapt to the Premier League. Even then, anything above £50m would pay for potential rather than production, and a 25% dribble success rate tells Arsenal he isn’t the specialist they need.

#1478. Alonso ready to sell £47m Chelsea signing for a Barca star

Chelsea transfer news: Xabi Alonso wants Barcelona right-back Jules Koundé at Chelsea and is ready to sell Marco Palestra, his £47m summer signing, to make room, according to El Nacional. The outlet says Alonso has pushed the case, a claim it credits to FourFourTwo, and that Palestra has Serie A interest from Juventus, AC Milan and Napoli, though it mentions no bid.

Barcelona would reportedly listen to offers of around €50m, roughly £43m, because Hansi Flick doesn’t treat Koundé as untouchable. The 28-year-old has started three of six LaLiga games this season after an ankle sprain on 17 October kept him out for over a month. El Nacional calls him a backup behind Eric García and says he’d welcome the move.

Koundé completes 93.9% of his passes, wins 58.8% of his duels and has 58 France caps, a composed defender who could play right-back or on the right of a back three. His body is the worry: a hamstring problem in March, then an ankle injury that lingered.

Palestra won Serie A’s Defender of the Year award at Cagliari, and his 81 completed dribbles topped every defender in Europe’s top five leagues. A thigh injury delayed his Chelsea debut until October, and El Nacional puts him at 202 minutes across six matches. Alonso prefers Josh Acheampong at right-back and, per BBC Sport, uses Palestra from the bench before Malo Gusto. He scored once in 37 league games, and his crossing remains modest.

Not as a swap. Palestra is a wing-back who beats opponents on the outside, while Koundé is a passer and cover defender best placed on the right of three centre-backs. Selling one doesn’t remove the need for the other, and Chelsea’s real shortage is right-sided cover: Reece James is injured and has been used in midfield, and Acheampong, a centre-back by trade, is filling in at right-back.

Koundé would solve that, but Gusto is the sale to make. He has lost his place, is reportedly open to a January exit, and Chelsea priced him at £75m in June, so even a discounted fee would cover much of Koundé’s £43m.

Selling Palestra after 202 minutes would mean writing off a player Alonso recruited and said needs time to adapt, to buy a 28-year-old with a muscle-injury record. Chelsea were fifth, 11 points behind Arsenal, before Leeds visited, without European football. Buy Koundé if the medical is clean, sell Gusto and keep Palestra.

#1477. Sunderland vs Jagiellonia Bialystok - prediction, team news, lineups

By Oliver Thomas | 24 Nov 2026 19:00, Last updated: 24 Nov 2026 21:37

Sunderland resume their Europa League campaign on Thursday night with a matchday five fixture against Polish outfit Jagiellonia Bialystok at the Stadium of Light.

While the Black Cats currently occupy 11th place in the 36-team League Phase standings, Jaga find themselves down in 27th place at the halfway stage.

Sunderland’s first major European campaign in 53 years began with back-to-back victories over AZ Alkmaar (1-0) and Torreense (2-1), but they have since suffered setbacks against Lech Poznan and Dinamo Zagreb.

Regis Le Bris’s men were held to a 1-1 draw in Poland by Poznan on matchday three before, they were booed off by the Stadium of Light faithful following a disappointing 2-0 home defeat three weeks ago, seeing them slip out of the automatic last-16 qualification spots.

Since then, Sunderland supporters have had a lot more to be optimistic about, with four points collected and two clean sheets kept in Premier League matches against Chelsea and Aston Villa, beating the former at home 1-0 before drawing 0-0 away against the latter last weekend.

The Black Cats remain inside the Premier League relegation zone, but a renewed sense of resilience has given Le Bris’s side something to build on. Their defensive home form has been particularly pleasing, keeping four clean sheets in their last six home matches across all competitions.

With a tricky trip to Italian giants AC Milan looming on matchday six, Le Bris might view this encounter against Jagiellonia as a must-win opportunity if they wish to climb back into the top eight and ensure they avoid a playoff place.

Competing in the Europa League for the first time in their history this term, Jagiellonia have endured a difficult start to their League Phase campaign, losing three of their first four matches to leave them sitting one point outside of the knockout round playoff places.

The 2024-25 Conference League quarter-finalists responded to a 2-1 opening defeat to Olympiacos with a 3-1 home victory over Ararat-Armenia, but they have since been brought back down to earth by successive losses without scoring against Anderlecht (3-0) and Levski Sofia (1-0).

Thirty-four-year-old boss Adrian Siemieniec is now ready to fulfil one of his coaching “dreams” by taking his Jagiellonia side to a Premier League stadium, with Thursday’s fixture against Sunderland representing one of their toughest tests yet on the continent.

Seeking to avoid a third straight away loss in Europe will be even more challenging without any away supporters, as Jaga were handed a UEFA ban following crowd disturbances in their most recent loss to Levski Sofia.

On the domestic front, Siemieniec recently acknowledged that his team’s form has fallen far below expectations this term, with seven wins and seven defeats posted in 14 Ekstraklasa matches. A 3-1 defeat at KS Cracovia last weekend leaves them down in ninth place in the table, six points behind the top three.

Although Trai Hume is one booking away from a European ban, he could continue on the right flank, unless Le Bris decides to recall either Malick Fofana or Nilson Angulo.

Enzo Le Fee has scored a team-high four goals this season – all penalties – and could operate in an advanced midfield role in front of Noah Sadiki and Jules Ahoka, while defensive trio Kevin Danso, Omar Alderete and Dayann Methalie will all be pushing to return after watching on as substitutes against Aston Villa.

As for Jagiellonia Bialystok, Ousmane Sow picked up a knock last weekend and has emerged as a doubt, but Norbert Wojtuszek recovered from injury to feature as an second-half substitute last time out and may be in a position to start at right-back ahead of Rodrigo Conceicao.

Jesus Imaz and Nik Prelec have scored seven goals each this term, but they are yet to make the net ripple in the Europa League this term. Nevertheless, the pair are strong contenders to start in centre-midfield and up front respectively.

#1476. Liverpool track Swedish left-back with £38m price tag

Liverpool transfer news: Liverpool are tracking Borussia Dortmund left-back Daniel Svensson, according to fussball-news.de, which names them and Arsenal as the most interested clubs.

Manchester United, Leeds, Milan, Juventus, Inter and Real Madrid are also watching the 24-year-old. Liverpool and Milan are reportedly preparing concrete steps for the winter window, although the report attributes no bid to either.

Dortmund will not make it easy. They want to keep a player contracted until June 2029 and plan to raise his salary, while Svensson feels settled and has no wish for a rushed move. A sale would cost at least €45m (about £38m), and Premier League clubs are ready to test Dortmund with a €30m (roughly £25m) offer, yet FotMob values him at just €23m.

The numbers explain the interest. Svensson has started all 10 Bundesliga games this season. His expected assists total of 1.13 comes without a single assist, and he has made 22 tackles, 14 interceptions and 45 recoveries while passing at 86.1%. He can play in midfield.

The flaws are clear. He has won only eight of 29 aerial duels and landed six of 32 crosses. He also plays as a wing-back in front of a back three, so Andoni Iraola’s back four would ask him to defend more of the flank alone.

Iraola’s 4-2-3-1 sends full-backs forward, and Milos Kerkez, bought for a reported £40m last year, has no goals or assists in the Premier League this season. Kostas Tsimikas, 30, is the backup on a contract that expires next year.

Not in January, and not at €45m. A €30m offer would fail, and £38m for a player FotMob values at €23m is poor business. Summer 2027 is the realistic window, once Tsimikas’s deal has run down.

The bigger problem sits on the other flank. Ronald Araujo, a centre-back by trade, is filling in at right-back while injuries have hit that position all season, so Iraola needs a natural right-back more urgently than a second left-back. Kerkez is 22 and signed until 2030, so Svensson would challenge him rather than replace him, which is healthy given Kerkez’s lack of end product.

Kerkez arrived with two Premier League seasons behind him, while Svensson would have to adapt to a new league and a new system. Liverpool should buy a right-back first and hold a ceiling of around £35m for Svensson, because above that they would repeat the Kerkez gamble with less evidence.

#1475. Watch: Amorim’s passionate ‘biggest mistake’ response which achieved viral status

Ruben Amorim’s response to a question regarding AC Milan’s squad building has gone viral on social media.

Given his past at Sporting CP, who are one of the three biggest clubs in Portugal, and Manchester United, arguably the biggest club in England, Amorim is no stranger to having his words in interviews and press conferences picked apart.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

In fact, we wrote at length about what his comments told us both before and after the derby win against Inter and the defeat to Ferencvaros. The Portuguese speaks his mind and leaves little to the imagination, doing so with clarity and often with charisma too.

A clip of one of the responses he gave in his pre-Frosinone presser has been doing the rounds on social media, gathering over two million views. When asked about the idea of spending money in January, Amorim’s reply was a typically impassioned one.

“That is the biggest mistakes of the big clubs: thinking that [we] look at the table. If we are near, let’s invest, crazy invest. If we are not near, let’s not invest. I think the key point is [to] have a long-term plan,” he said.

“If you lose all the games, sack the manager – that is normal (smiles). I’m not talking about that. But what I’m saying is that: stick with your plan. We have a plan. What kind of player we want. [One who] is able to make all the runs that we want. He has the character that we want.

“Not a big star – like a guy that is composed and come here to be one of the part of the team. If we have that really clear and we go for the best that we can. Young, old – it’s better young in this moment. But if you have a clear plan, don’t look at the table.

“Look at the table to evaluate the process, but to buy, to spend money for the five next years, don’t look at the table. And I think that is the biggest mistake of the clubs: like putting all the [effort into] trying to be champion by spending money. That is the biggest mistake.

“So we have a clear plan. It doesn’t matter the table. We are going to address what we want in a very clear way. So that is not going to change. And I look at the table. I look at our players… we can do better.

“Can we win against Ferencvaros, a very good team? Can we play better against that team? We can, with our players. So we have a clear process. So we are not going to change what we want because we look at the table in December or in January. So we have a clear plan what to do.”

“We have a CLEAR long-term plan and we won’t change it because of the table.”

“We want players with the right CHARACTER — not BIG STARS. Young is better right now.”

#1474. Juventus boss reacts to Manchester United’s midfield link: Is he worth £28m?

Tuttomercato carries Luciano Spalletti’s reaction to the talk linking Weston McKennie with Manchester United, and the Juventus head coach played it down. He spoke to the midfielder as soon as the story broke and didn’t think McKennie had hinted at wanting to leave, calling his comments a general remark. Spalletti said their relationship is as good as the one he has with everybody else, and everything felt calm once McKennie returned from international duty.

Those comments came from McKennie himself, who suggested during USMNT camp that Mauricio Pochettino could bring American players to Old Trafford. La Gazzetta dello Sport then reported that United’s new head coach wants him in January, though McKennie says he isn’t planning to leave and Fabrizio Romano insists United aren’t working on a deal.

Pochettino inherits a club in trouble: one win and eight points from ten league games, 18th place and Michael Carrick’s sacking after their worst league start in 40 years. The Argentine takes charge at Anfield today, before Wednesday’s Champions League trip to Sporting CP.

McKennie, 28, offers versatility: Spalletti has used him on both wings, at wing-back and even as a striker, and he managed eight goals and five assists in 38 appearances before signing his new deal in March. This season the output has dipped, with FotMob showing one goal, no assists and a 6.98 rating from eight Serie A starts. His contract runs to 2030, and FotMob values him at about £28m.

Not as a January priority. United’s problem is a team that loses control of matches, and McKennie is a runner who arrives in the box rather than a midfielder who dictates tempo. Put him next to a struggling back four and his versatility becomes a drawback, because Spalletti gets the best from him higher up the pitch, where his goals come from.

Pochettino’s trust is a real advantage, since he knows exactly what work rate he gets, but trust doesn’t turn a 28-year-old with one league goal this season into a £28m solution to a defensive crisis. Juventus also just rewarded him with a contract to 2030, so they have no reason to sell cheaply.

Romano mentioned Youri Tielemans, Carlos Baleba and Andrey Santos in the same breath, and each offers more control from midfield. If Pochettino wants a familiar face, a rotation option on a short deal makes sense. Spending about £28m on a runner does not.

#1473. Tottenham join race for Inter midfielder facing pay cut: Right move for Spurs?

Tottenham transfer news: Tottenham Hotspur are one of four clubs tracking Hakan Calhanoglu, according to Tuttomercatoweb. The Italian outlet lists Galatasaray, Juventus and Como alongside Spurs, although it gives no detail on how far Tottenham’s interest has progressed.

The timing matters because the Inter midfielder’s contract expires on 30 June 2027, which lets him agree a pre-contract with a foreign club from January. Inter want to extend but are trimming wages for their over-30s. Calhanoglu earns roughly £5.7m a year, and Inter are discussing £4.4m plus bonuses. He prefers to stay but hopes to avoid a heavy cut, and no formal offer exists yet.

Calhanoglu turns 33 in February. FotMob shows three goals in 485 minutes from nine Serie A appearances, 91.4% pass accuracy, 20 chances created and a 98th-percentile ranking for shot attempts among Serie A central midfielders.

Passing range, long-distance shooting and dead-ball quality remain his strengths. He wins only 44.4% of his duels, though, completes a quarter of his dribbles, and his recovery speed will keep dropping with age. FotMob values him at about £6.4m, down from a £39m peak in 2024.

Roberto De Zerbi wants his midfield to dictate play from deep, which suits Calhanoglu’s skills. Spurs have 15 points from 11 league games after beating Ipswich 2-0 on Saturday, their fourth win in five. Yet Sandro Tonali (£100m) and Mateus Fernandes (£85m) joined in July, and Rodrigo Bentancur, Conor Gallagher and Archie Gray compete for the same places.

Not as a priority. Money isn’t the obstacle. Tonali reportedly earns more than £275,000 a week, so Calhanoglu’s wages would barely register, and a free transfer costs no fee. Squad space is the problem. Spurs bought Tonali and Fernandes to run De Zerbi’s base for years, and a 33-year-old in the same role would either sit on the bench or take minutes from Gray and Lucas Bergvall, whom the club needs to develop.

Spurs would also struggle to sell the project without European football, while Galatasaray can reportedly offer higher wages. The case only strengthens if Tonali or Bentancur leaves, or if De Zerbi wants a penalty and set-piece specialist. Neither applies now, and nothing forces Spurs to act in January.

Calhanoglu’s output is real, but it comes with a decline in athleticism that a 33-year-old can’t reverse. Spurs would be paying for a short-term fix in a position where they have already invested £185m in the long-term answer.

#1472. Ferrero sets Juventus ambition to be what it once was, as €200m capital raise runs

Juventus president Gianluca Ferrero set out the leadership's view of the rebuild at the Brussels launch of the club's European Union fan club. He spoke while a capital raise of about €200m is open and a UEFA settlement limits spending.

Juventus president Gianluca Ferrero went to Brussels on 18 November with a clear message for supporters. Restoring the club to its former self is its absolute ambition, he said, adding that the club is following the path set out by its chief executive and is confident this can happen. He spoke at the opening of the Juventus Official Fan Club European Union, which is chaired by MEP Sandro Gozi. The timing gives the statement weight.

The new supporters’ club opened at the Iosono il Piemonte event space. Its stated purpose is to link Juventus supporters with the institutional centre of Europe.

Before the opening, the delegation went to the European Parliament with Gozi. Chief Club Affairs Officer Giorgio Chiellini led the group alongside Ferrero. Piedmont regional president Alberto Cirio attended the opening, as did MEPs who have joined the fan club.

The visit showed Chiellini’s work on the club’s relations with institutions and European football. It also gives supporters an official club in Brussels.

The financial backdrop is demanding. Juventus posted a consolidated loss of €66m for 2025/26. On 12 November, the board approved the offer, using part of the €250m authority granted by shareholders at the extraordinary meeting on 3 November.

The offer involves up to 208.5m new shares at €0.96 each. Shareholders can buy one new share for every two they hold. The price is 28.36% below the theoretical ex-rights price, based on that day’s share price. The remaining €50m of the authority can be used in later financial years, depending on the club’s financial needs and investment plans.

The spending limits come from UEFA. European football’s governing body fined Juventus €20m for breaking the football earnings rule. Of that amount, €14m is conditional. The club agreed a three-year settlement with annual targets. It also faces limits on registering new players on its UEFA List A.

Those are the limits within which Ferrero’s ambition must be pursued. Any improvement in the squad has to fit within the annual targets agreed with UEFA.

Subscription rights can be traded on Euronext Milan until 25 November, and the offer closes on 1 December 2026.

#1471. Doubts over Olise and Musiala as Bayern target three rising Premier League stars

By Alexis Pereira | 24 Nov 2026 19:18

Bayern Munich have doubts over the long-term futures of Michael Olise and Jamal Musiala and are reportedly considering three Premier League wingers. After securing Harry Kane’s extension until June 2029, the Munich hierarchy now have two more delicate cases to handle.

The first is Olise, who has attracted interest from Real Madrid and Barcelona. Arsenal have just joined the list of suitors, while Liverpool and Manchester City are also following his situation. Bayern want to extend the French star’s contract, which currently runs until 2029, but no agreement has yet been found.

The Bavarian club also have doubts over Musiala’s long-term future. According to TeamTalk, several Bayern officials are said to question his ability to regain his best level, as the German attacking midfielder suffers absences linked to a ‘neurological dysfunction’.

The British outlet reveals that Bayern are following three Premier League players closely. The first is Liverpool’s young prospect Rio Ngumoha. The 18-year-old winger’s profile appeals to the German hierarchy, but Liverpool are reportedly close to signing him to a new long-term deal, which would seriously complicate Bayern’s ambitions.

The Munich club are also said to be keeping an eye on Florian Wirtz. Already highly rated in Germany after his rise at Bayer Leverkusen, the 23-year-old Germany international remains a prime target, though his importance to Liverpool makes a transfer hard to bring about.

Vincent Kompany is also said to have noted the name of his compatriot Jeremy Doku. The Belgian manager knows the Manchester City winger well, but there is a snag: the 24-year-old extended his contract with City until June 2031 this summer.

Bayern therefore appear to be at a disadvantage in signing any of these three rising Premier League stars, unless there is a dramatic turnaround. At the same time, the German side are also reportedly studying Bundesliga solutions, following Ibrahim Maza, Said El Mala and Antonio Nusa.

#1470. Manchester City’s £31m left-back wanted in Turin: Loan or sale in January?

CalcioMercato reports that Juventus have started monitoring Rayan Aït-Nouri ahead of the transfer market reopening, and the Manchester City left-back seems ready to listen. The Algeria international wants to restart his career elsewhere, views Turin favourably and has told his entourage to strengthen contacts, while the interest from Juventus is real and the club intends to act soon to test the deal’s feasibility.

City want to sell outright and reinvest immediately, whereas Juventus prefer a loan with an option to buy, which suits a club bound by a UEFA settlement agreement. They first asked in August and City refused, while Gazzetta dello Sport says Luciano Spalletti wants competition for Andrea Cambiaso.

City paid Wolves a reported £31m in June 2025 and gave him a contract until 2030, yet Enzo Maresca reportedly ranks the 25-year-old behind Joško Gvardiol and Nico O’Reilly. He had played 168 minutes in all competitions by mid-November, none of them in the Premier League, and his only starts have come in the EFL Cup.

His strengths explain the fee. Aït-Nouri scored nine goals and set up 15 in 135 Premier League games for Wolves, added five assists in 1,605 minutes last season, and can also operate in central areas.

The weakness is defensive security, because he is an ultra-attacking left-back. That matters now, with City on one point from their last four league games after losing 3-1 at Nottingham Forest and drawing 1-1 with Fulham on Saturday.

No, not in January, and not on terms that leave City carrying all the risk. Maresca has used Nico O’Reilly in midfield this season, yet O’Reilly started only seven of City’s first 15 games while managing a back problem, so an available specialist left-back is no luxury. Khusanov, Nunes and Guéhi all picked up knocks at Forest, which leaves the back line short.

City should treat the Juventus talks as a pricing exercise. A straight loan sends a 25-year-old on a contract until 2030 away for six months and returns him no more valuable, so only a loan with an obligation to buy close to the £31m fee makes sense.

Otherwise, give him a league start, see whether his attacking threat helps a side that keeps conceding, and let Maresca’s evidence decide. A club that paid £31m for a left-back last year has not shown he cannot do the job; it has shown only that the manager prefers somebody else.

#1469. Arsenal eye Serie A’s 11-goal striker: Should they pay £26m?

Arsenal transfer news from Italy centres on Monza striker Gustavo Varela, with Gianluca Di Marzio reportingthat the Gunners are very interested. The 21-year-old Portugal forward has scored 11 goals in 11 Serie A games since joining from Benfica B in July. Barcelona are equally keen, Inter watch him live at every match, and Napoli are reported as his strongest Italian suitor.

The interest makes sense. Viktor Gyokeres, signed for £64m in 2025, has two goals in 15 appearances and none in the Premier League, while Kai Havertz has started 10 of 11 league games for three goals. Arsenal’s results haven’t suffered, but their number nine position has produced little.

Finishing is the selling point. FotMob‘s data has him scoring well above his expected goals for a Monza side that won only two of its first 10 league games, and he averages around three shots per 90 minutes. The weaknesses are just as clear: he wins 34% of his duels, completes 41% of his dribbles and ranks in the ninth percentile among forwards for defensive contribution, which clashes with the pressing Arteta wants from his striker.

Di Marzio says Monza will listen at around £22m to £26m, with the money earmarked for other signings, after paying about £3m including bonuses. Flashscore reports Benfica hold a 20% sell-on and a right to match offers, and Varela’s agents meet Monza this week.

Yes, but in the summer and only if Gyokeres leaves. Arsenal’s results are strong, so a January rush for a 21-year-old would add risk without fixing a crisis. A fee near £26m looks modest beside the £64m Gyokeres cost, and Varela’s goals-per-game record argues for the gamble far more than Gyokeres’ two in 15 does.

The real risk is suitability. He also scores for a struggling side, so his chances come in games unlike most of the Premier League games Arsenal play. Arteta needs a number nine who presses and wins duels, and Varela does neither well, so Arsenal would be buying a finisher and building the rest of his game themselves.

That is workable if Varela arrives as competition for Havertz rather than the first choice. Arsenal should also expect resistance beyond the price, because Benfica’s matching right and Inter’s summer plans complicate any early bid.

Watching him until June costs Arsenal nothing, and another 20 league games will show whether this form is real or a hot streak.

Manchester United defender Ayden Heaven is reportedly open to leaving the 20-time English champions on loan during the January transfer window.

Heaven, 20, has made eight appearances for the Red Devils this season, including five outings in the Premier League, but he was an unused substitute against Liverpool on Sunday.

Man United are expected to target a new defender during the January transfer window due to their problems in that area of the field.

The Red Devils have conceded 34 times across all competitions this season, which is the worst defensive record in Europe's top five leagues.

According to BBC Sport, Heaven has concerns over what Man United's current struggles could mean for his development.

Heaven allegedly accepts that current head coach Mauricio Pochettino is likely to turn to more experienced options, as the Red Devils face a battle against relegation from the Premier League.

The Englishman has a contract at Old Trafford until the summer of 2029, but it is understood that he would be willing to leave the club on a permanent basis if the right opportunity arrived.

Fulham's Calvin Bassey and Brentford's Nathan Collins are believed to be January options for Man United to boost their defensive unit.

Heaven arrived at Man United from Arsenal in February 2025, and he has represented the 20-time English champions on 32 occasions in all competitions.

#1467. Kean’s new tibia injury rules former Juventus striker out of Como v Juventus

Moise Kean has broken down again in Como training, three weeks after treatment that was meant to fix his shin. The former Juventus striker is set to miss about two more months, so he will not face his old club on 29 November.

Moise Kean has suffered a new tibia injury in training with Como. The former Juventus striker is now undergoing further medical tests. Sky Sport Italia reported that he will be out for about two more months. That timeline rules him out of Como’s home game against Juventus.

Como’s statement of 17 November gave no recovery date. The club promised an update once more information was available.

The new problem follows a treatment that was meant to end his shin trouble. On 30 October, Como’s update described his treatment at the Cugat Institute in Barcelona as successful. The club put his recovery at about five weeks. His progress was to be reviewed every day.

That plan has now collapsed. Kean had been out since early October. The original injury came while he was playing for Italy against France on 2 October. That match was the first leg of a Nations League tie.

The setback is a heavy blow for Como. In Serie A, his outings for the club added up to 160 minutes. He has yet to score, including in his single Champions League game. He joined from Fiorentina on an initial loan, with an obligation to make the move permanent. At Fiorentina he scored 27 league goals in two seasons, 19 of them in 2024/25. Before that, he came through the Juventus academy.

Without him, Como will have to rely on Douvikas up front. The club may also look for a striker in January.

For Juventus, the news removes one threat from a crucial stretch. Como are their next opponents after Venezia. The game is the Sunday evening fixture a week later, in round 13 of Serie A. Kick-off is at 20:45.

#1466. CM: Gimenez could terminate Porto loan early and return to Milan – the situation

Santiago Gimenez left AC Milan in the summer, but he may be returning before the end of his loan deal next summer.

It’s fair to say that Gimenez is one of the most difficult signings to assess from Milan in recent years. On paper, it made plenty of sense why he was right to arrive; he was firing in the Champions League, he had no difficulty scoring in the league and there was the added bonus of him being young and a fan of the club.

With goals against elite teams in Europe too, it made sense why he’d be able to have a successful career at San Siro. Performing on the biggest stage seemingly wasn’t an issue.

So, when he started brightly, fans thought the Rossoneri had struck gold. Yet, that form quickly came undone and Gimenez began to show glimpses, rather than actually developing a portfolio of goalscoring.

After almost being forced out of the club last summer, an injury-ridden campaign effectively ended his time with the Diavolo and he was loaned out in the summer. Yet, he could already be heading back to Italy.

As Calciomercato.com writes, it’s highly unlikely that Porto will activate the €18m buy clause in his deal, and it’s even possible that he doesn’t see out the complete spell of his loan. He’s the third-choice striker, with only four appearances in the Portuguese top flight and one penalty goal; it’s hardly form that warrants making his stay permanent.

Now, ahead of the January mercato, a meeting is planned with Rafaela Pimenta to discuss what would be best for his career. A return to Milanello cannot be ruled out, but it wouldn’t be permanent. He’s not part of Ruben Amorim’s plans, so a new destination would need to be found.

What is for sure, though, is that his value has only dropped further with his Portuguese adventure…

#1465. Chelsea’s England playmaker on Man Utd’s radar

Chelsea transfer news around Cole Palmer has flared again, with Mauricio Pochettino’s arrival at Manchester United reviving the noise. Reporter Dean Jones insists the England playmaker’s future at Stamford Bridge is not in doubt, but he admits the sentiment around it is becoming harder to ignore.

Palmer, a boyhood United supporter, has been linked with Old Trafford before. United appointed Pochettino on 18 November after sacking Michael Carrick following one win in ten league games. The Argentine made Palmer one of his most used players at Chelsea, where the pair built a positive relationship, and Palmer scored 22 league goals in 2023/24.

Jones rates the chances of Palmer joining United as extremely low. United’s January budget stands at roughly £50m, and they want a left-back, a centre-back and a striker. A player FotMob values at €100m, roughly £87m, sits outside both the money and the shopping list. Jones also sees no sign that Palmer wants to leave, and says relations at Stamford Bridge would need to break down badly first.

Palmer has started all 11 of Chelsea’s Premier League games this season, playing 970 minutes for three goals, one from the penalty spot, and three assists. His 23 chances created include six big chances, and his 2.58 expected goals backs up the output. Xabi Alonso says, “The better Cole we have, the better Chelsea we have”.

Only ten of Palmer’s 31 shots have hit the target; he wins 46.9% of his dribbles, and he has collected two yellows and a red. Fitness worries more after an injury-hit 2025/26 that ended with him missing the World Cup.

No, but Chelsea should treat Jones’s condition as the real warning. Palmer’s contract runs to 2034, and United’s budget does not reach his valuation, so the danger lies in a deteriorating relationship, not a bid. That puts the onus on Alonso, Chelsea’s seventh permanent manager since 2021.

Morgan Rogers’ £117m arrival from Aston Villa creates the obvious flashpoint. If Palmer feels crowded out of the number ten role, or pushed wide right too often, the homesickness talk will return. Clear roles and managed minutes will protect him better than another forward.

The money belongs elsewhere. Alonso’s side beat United 2-0 on 31 October, then lost 1-0 at Sunderland eight days later, and defensive brittleness and thin squad depth keep undermining a front line that already scores. A back line that leaks goals will not.

#1464. Union SG vs Lech Poznan - prediction, team news, lineups

By Saikat Mandal | 24 Nov 2026 19:25, Last updated: 24 Nov 2026 20:48

Union SG will be looking to maintain their impressive Europa League form when they host Lech Poznan at King Power at Den Dreef Stadium on Thursday.

The Old Lady remain unbeaten in the competition and sit fourth in the standings, while the visitors are languishing second from bottom in the table.

The Belgian side began their Europa League campaign with a convincing 3-0 victory over Viktoria Plzen away from home and have since collected 10 points from four matches, scoring 10 goals in the process.

The only occasion on which they dropped points came against Real Sociedad, when David Hubert's side fought back from behind to secure a 1-1 draw.

A scintillating second-half display helped them to a commanding 4-0 victory over Hapoel Be'er Sheva, while Union followed that up with a 2-1 triumph over Celta Vigo on matchday four.

They are unbeaten in their last 16 matches and head into this encounter on the back of seven consecutive victories across all competitions, a run that should give them plenty of confidence.

USG are also setting the pace in the Pro League, sitting top of the table with 32 points from 12 matches, having recorded 10 wins and two draws without tasting defeat.

Lech Poznan comfortably dispatched Swiss side Thun 9-2 on aggregate to secure their place in the Europa League league phase, but they have since struggled to find their feet in the competition.

The Railwaymen began their campaign with a 4-0 defeat to Crystal Palace before suffering another heavy loss by the same scoreline against Bayer Leverkusen.

The Polish side ground out a hard-fought 1-1 draw against Sunderland, but Benfica proved too strong in their next outing, handing them a 3-1 defeat on matchday four.

Having scored just two goals and conceded 14, they are among the three teams languishing near the bottom of the table with only one point, with only FC Ararat-Armenia faring worse.

Lech Poznan, however, have been outstanding domestically, sitting top of the league with 35 points from 14 matches, four clear of Gornik despite having played a game fewer.

Union SG are currently without Mateo Biondic, who is struggling with a knee injury, while Kevin Mac Allister has been ruled out for the remainder of the season with an ACL injury.

Hubert could make several changes to the side that faced Kortrijk in their last league outing, with Nikki Havenaar potentially coming into a three-man defence and Louis Patris moving into midfield.

Besfort Zeneli, who scored twice against Celta Vigo, is likely to return to the starting lineup in place of Darius Olaru, while Kevin Rodríguez is expected to lead the line.

Lech Poznan, meanwhile, are likely to adopt a more cautious approach away from home, with Niels Frederiksen potentially setting his side up in a 4-2-3-1 formation, with Yannick Agnero operating as the lone striker.

Mateusz Pruchniewski has been ruled out for the rest of the season with an ACL injury, while Ali Gholizadeh is still recovering from the same problem and is unlikely to return before January.

Alex Douglas is sidelined with a broken rib, while Joao Moutinho is not expected to return before February. However, Pablo Rodriguez and Mikael Ishak have both returned to training.

#1463. Liverpool lining up Ajax teenager for January

Liverpool transfer news from Goal says Ajax teenager Abdellah Ouazane is a January target as attacking cover for Florian Wirtz. Julian Ward, Liverpool’s recruitment chief, has reportedly sped up plans to support the £116m playmaker, and Ouazane has become a serious option before the winter window opens. Wael Mohya and Gilberto Mora sit on the same shortlist.

The 17-year-old grew up supporting Liverpool and badly wants to play at Anfield. Ajax hold the leverage, though: his contract runs to 2028, and persuading them to sell a prized academy graduate mid-season will take careful negotiation. De Telegraaf also reported earlier this season that sporting director Jordi Cruyff wants to give him a new deal when he turns 18 on 15 January.

Ouazane is mainly an attacking midfielder who also plays wide or up front. FotMob‘s 2026/27 numbers show two goals and one assist in 12 Eredivisie games, only four of them starts, across 441 minutes. His goals and shot attempts rank in the 88th and 86th percentiles among comparable attackers.

The gaps are just as clear: he sits in the 19th percentile for defensive contributions and the 15th for aerial duels won, and a 45.7% dribble success rate suggests he still loses the ball too often against senior opponents. Real Madrid pulled out of a 2025 deal after his medical, though Ajax’s own checks cleared him.

Iraola’s Liverpool press harder and play more direct than they did under Arne Slot, so that defensive profile matters. Wirtz works as the central creator with Bradley Barcola, Victor Munoz and Rio Ngumoha out wide, which leaves the number 10 role as Ouazane’s only route in.

Yes, but as a planned investment rather than genuine cover. Wirtz missed several matches with a back problem last February, so depth behind him is a fair concern. Yet Liverpool sit fourth, a point behind second-placed Brighton after Sunday’s 4-0 win over Manchester United, and only eighth in the Champions League table after losing to Fenerbahce. January minutes will decide those races, and Ouazane has four Eredivisie starts and numbers that clash with Iraola’s pressing.

His lifelong Anfield dream and Ward’s record of targeting elite teenagers give Liverpool an edge, so they should push. If Ajax demand a premium for a mid-season exit, Ward should wait for the summer, when Liverpool can judge a full Eredivisie campaign. Four starts make him a bet on 2028, not insurance for February.

#1462. Braga vs KuPS - prediction, team news, lineups

By Adeyeye Oluwapelumi | 24 Nov 2026 19:40

Braga will look to strengthen their position in the Conference League knockout-stage race when they welcome KuPS Kuopio to the Estadio Municipal de Braga on Thursday evening.

Franclim Carvalho's side are 17th in the 36-team standings with four points from three matches, while the Finnish visitors sit 33rd with just one point after failing to win any of their opening three European outings.

Despite going unbeaten in their six matches across three Conference League qualifying rounds (W4, D2) and keeping clean sheets in all of them, Braga have found life in the league phase considerably more challenging.

The Archbishops began their campaign with a disappointing 3-0 defeat away to Copenhagen before responding with a 2-0 home victory over Gent on matchday two, giving Carvalho his first win since replacing the sacked Carlos Vicens in October.

However, Braga were unable to build on that success in their latest continental outing, playing out a goalless draw away to Aarhus, although the new manager can take encouragement from the defensive improvements made in recent times.

The Portuguese outfit are unbeaten in their last four matches across all competitions, keeping clean sheets in each and winning three, with their latest success coming in a 2-0 victory away to Vitoria de Guimaraes in the Taca de Portugal at the weekend.

That result followed a 1-0 league win at Rio Ave, leaving Braga eighth in the Primeira Liga table with 17 points from their opening 11 fixtures and three points adrift of the top five.

The Archbishops are also three points away from fifth place in the Conference League standings, with several teams between 10th and 14th sitting just two points ahead, meaning maximum points on Thursday could strengthen their hopes of securing a top-eight finish.

Braga have plenty of reason to feel confident ahead of the contest, having won 14 of their last 16 home matches in European competition (D1, L1) and kept 12 clean sheets during that run.

KuPS, meanwhile, have struggled to make an impression in their second consecutive Conference League league-phase campaign, losing 4-2 to Trabzonspor in their opening fixture before suffering a 2-0 defeat away to Borac Banja Luka on matchday two.

The Finnish side collected their first point with a goalless draw against Gent on matchday three, but that result did little to disguise their attacking struggles, having scored just twice and conceded six goals across their opening three matches in the competition.

Miika Nuutinen's men have also gone seven matches without a victory, including a 1-1 draw against Swedish side Norrkoping in a friendly on November 19, while their most recent competitive outing was a 2-0 home defeat to Inter Turku in their final match of the 2026 top-flight campaign.

That result left the Yellow-Blacks third in the Veikkausliiga table, meaning they missed out on retaining the domestic title they won last season but secured a place in the first qualifying round of the Conference League.

KuPS have also struggled on their travels, recording just one victory in their last eight competitive away matches and failing to win any of their most recent four, three of which ended in defeat.

Braga will be without Sikou Niakate, who is recovering from a ruptured Achilles tendon that has kept him sidelined since April.

Jonas Wind is also doubtful after missing the recent victory over Vitoria because of physical overload, while Gabriel Silva returned as a second-half substitute at the weekend after missing the previous four matches through fitness problems and could feature again as he builds up his match fitness.

Fran Navarro ended a more than three-month wait for a goal by scoring against Vitoria and is expected to retain his place at the head of the attack, with club captain Ricardo Horta and Pau Victor also likely to feature in Carvalho's forward line.

KuPS could be without 22-year-old Ghanaian winger Bob Nii Armah, who picked up an injury during the goalless draw with Gent.

Thirty-three-year-old attacker Piotr Parzyszek has started all three of the Finnish side's league-phase matches and could retain his place despite failing to score in his last 10 competitive appearances for the club.

B Fontes; V Gomez, Lagerbielke, Barisic, Travassos; Gorby, Dorgeles, Moutinho; P Victor, Navarro, Horta

Kreidl; Savolainen, Hamalainen, Lotjonen, Kujasalo; Gasc, Pasanen; Aiki, Pennanen, Eskesen; Parzyszek

KuPS have managed just two goals in three Conference League matches and enter this encounter without a win in six outings, while Braga have won three of their last four matches and kept clean sheets in all of them, making a home victory the most likely outcome.

#1461. Como beat Cagliari 2-0 to go back into fourth, eight points clear of next opponents Juventus

Como beat Cagliari 2-0 with two headers from Yan Couto crosses, moving back into fourth place on 26 points. Juventus visit next and trail the side holding the last Champions League place by eight points.

Como beat Cagliari 2-0 at the Stadio Giuseppe Sinigaglia on Saturday, 21 November 2026. Both goals were headers, and Yan Couto crossed for both of them. The result lifted Fàbregas’ side back into fourth place. That is the last Champions League place, and Juventus are the next visitors.

Ramón opened the scoring after 24 minutes. He met Couto’s cross from the right and headed past goalkeeper Caprile. Da Cunha, the captain, doubled the lead in the 56th minute. He headed in another Couto delivery from the centre of the area.

Fàbregas left Nico Paz and Perrone on the bench. The two Argentinians had rejoined the squad only hours before kick-off after international duty. Como play AEK in the Champions League on Tuesday. Even without the pair from the start, the hosts kept Cagliari out. Both men entered in the 57th minute, with Liberali and Milla making way respectively. It was Como’s first win since a defeat to Inter before the international break.

For Fàbregas, the performance was not perfect, but he was very pleased. Perrone had a minor problem, the coach explained, which ruled out a full 90 minutes for the midfielder.

Como have now won three Serie A home games in a row without conceding, which they last did in October and November 1984, according to Sportmediaset. Da Cunha has three goals in his last four games across Serie A and the Champions League. Fàbregas has never lost to Cagliari in five Serie A matches as a coach. He has won three of them and drawn two. Cagliari have lost each of their last four away league games. That is their first run of four straight away defeats in Serie A since November–December 2023.

Como have eight wins, two draws and two defeats from 12 games, according to Como 1907. They have scored 20 goals and conceded 10.

In that table, Juventus’ record reads five wins, three draws and three defeats. They have scored 15 goals and conceded 12. The gap to Como stood at eight points before Juventus’ game against Venezia.

Juventus have played one game fewer. Even so, Como have scored more and conceded fewer. Juventus will face a side whose crossing from the right produced both goals on Saturday.

Como face AEK first. After that European tie, attention turns to the visit of Juventus. The Bianconeri travel to the Sinigaglia on Sunday 29 November, with kick-off set for 20:45 CET.
